records.title: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CJ — macro-Pythagorean joint-pair occupancy floor and nested-selector necessity
records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CJ — macro-Pythagorean joint-pair occupancy floor and nested-selector necessity
STATUS: POST_229CI_MACRO_JOINT_PAIR_AUDIT / EXPLICIT_LARGE_COMMON_RADICAL_FAMILY / JOINT_PAIR_OCCUPANCY_FLOOR / MACRO_ONLY_CROSS_SELECTOR_ATTACK_NO_GO / NESTED_PHYSICAL_SELECTORS_REQUIRED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
CARD_DOC_ID=1CXfuP3IGbzhgY_QN3W4vmESEvH7Nae7MteNIxsDSxyo
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CI
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope


Retain 229CI on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) source:
Sigma_xy=rad(xy),
Sigma_R=rad(eR),
kappa=rad(G0)=gcd(Sigma_xy,Sigma_R),
Sigma_xy=kappa A_xy,
Sigma_R=kappa A_R,
with kappa,A_xy,A_R pairwise-coprime squarefree and, on J>K,
A_xy A_R>K/3.


Retain the exact macro-Pythagorean identity
(eR)^2+(xy)^2=(UV)^2.
For physical endpoints R<=B, all three macro coordinates are <=B^2.


229CI proved that the two receivers cannot be counted separately using only their own single-Pythagorean hosts.
This card tests the next weaker possibility:
can the JOINT pair be counted using only
(i) one scaled Pythagorean equation,
(ii) macro height <=B^2,
(iii) common radical kappa>T,
(iv) pairwise-coprime residual radicals,
(v) A_xy A_R>K/3?


The answer is no. An explicit ambient macro-Pythagorean family already has far more than B^(1/3) such joint radical pairs.


2. Abstract macro host


Let T=B^(1/3-delta), with fixed 0<delta<1/3.


Consider positive integer triples
X^2+Y^2=Z^2,
Z<=B^2.
Put
G=gcd(X,Y),
kappa=rad(G),
Sigma_X=rad(X),
Sigma_Y=rad(Y),
A_X=Sigma_X/kappa,
A_Y=Sigma_Y/kappa,
whenever gcd(Sigma_X,Sigma_Y)=kappa.


Every Stage37 physical pair
(X,Y,Z)=(eR,xy,UV)
lies in this ambient macro host, with G=G0 and
(Sigma_X,Sigma_Y)=(Sigma_R,Sigma_xy).


No converse is claimed.


3. Explicit fixed-kappa family


For all sufficiently large B, choose one odd prime q with
2T<q<4T.
Such q exists by Bertrand's postulate after replacing 2T by a neighboring integer if necessary.


Put
M=floor(B/(16 q^(3/2))).
Then M tends to infinity and M/q tends to infinity.


For each prime s in
M<=s<=3M/2,
set
m=2qs, n=1.
Since m is even and gcd(m,n)=1, the standard Euclid triple
L_1=2mn=4qs,
L_2=m^2-n^2=4q^2s^2-1,
H=m^2+n^2=4q^2s^2+1
is primitive.


Scale it by q:
X_s=4q^2s,
Y_s=q(4q^2s^2-1),
Z_s=q(4q^2s^2+1).                                      (CJ.1)


Then
X_s^2+Y_s^2=Z_s^2,
gcd(X_s,Y_s)=q.                                         (CJ.2)


The height is admissible:
for s<=3M/2,
4q^3s^2 <= 9B^2/256,
hence
Z_s<B^2
for all sufficiently large B.                            (CJ.3)


Thus the entire family lives inside the same macro box that contains the Stage37 physical product triple.


4. Exact joint radical decomposition in the family


Because q and s are distinct odd primes for large B,
Sigma_X(s)=rad(X_s)=2qs.                                  (CJ.4)


Also
Y_s=q(4q^2s^2-1),
where
4q^2s^2-1 is odd,
is congruent to -1 modulo q,
and is congruent to -1 modulo s.


Hence
Sigma_Y(s)=q rad(4q^2s^2-1),                              (CJ.5)
and exactly
gcd(Sigma_X(s),Sigma_Y(s))=q.                             (CJ.6)


Therefore
kappa=q>T,                                                (CJ.7)
A_X(s)=2s,
A_Y(s)=rad(4q^2s^2-1),                                   (CJ.8)
and
q,A_X(s),A_Y(s)
are pairwise coprime squarefree.


Moreover
A_X(s)A_Y(s)>=2s.                                         (CJ.9)


In particular at the current balanced J cutoff
K=T^(1/5),
we have
A_X(s)A_Y(s)>K/3
for all sufficiently large B.                             (CJ.10)


So the explicit family satisfies all of the support-level hypotheses retained by the 229CI joint-pair contract, except the genuinely nested Stage37 physical selectors.


5. Joint occupied-pair floor


The pairs
(Sigma_X(s),Sigma_Y(s))
are distinct as s varies, because the first coordinate is exactly 2qs.


By the prime number theorem,
#{s prime:M<=s<=3M/2}
 >> M/log M
 >> B q^(-3/2)/log B
 >> B T^(-3/2)/log B
 = B^(1/2+(3/2)delta)/log B.                       (CJ.11)


Therefore the ambient macro host contains
>> B^(1/2+(3/2)delta)/log B
distinct JOINT radical pairs satisfying
kappa>T,
pairwise-coprime residuals,
and the balanced residual-product condition.


RESULT_229CJ_MACRO_PYTHAGOREAN_JOINT_PAIR_OCCUPANCY_FLOOR=
B^(1/2+(3/2)delta-o(1)).


In particular this is far above B^(1/3), so no theorem based only on the macro-Pythagorean relation, macro height, common radical and residual-product constraints can supply the required one-third occupied-pair bound.


RESULT_229CJ_MACRO_ONLY_DUAL_RADICAL_OCCUPANCY_ATTACK=QUANTITATIVELY_FALSE.


6. Scope firewall


The family (CJ.1) is NOT claimed to admit factorizations
X=eR,
Y=xy,
Z=UV
coming from one simultaneous Stage37 physical endpoint.
It is not an endpoint lower bound.


The conclusion is a method firewall:
229CI's phrase "same-physical cross-selector correlation" must use more than the macro identity
(eR)^2+(xy)^2=(UV)^2.


The missing useful information must come from the nested simultaneous system itself, for example
x^2+y^2=z^2,
e^2+z^2=R^2,
e^2+x^2=U^2,
e^2+y^2=V^2,
the exact content charts, lambda_i^2 routers, or an equivalent bounded-fiber incidence theorem preserving all of them.


7. Updated theorem contract


Supersede the weaker interpretation
J_DUAL_RADICAL_CROSS_SELECTOR_OCCUPANCY = "count the pair using the macro Pythagorean equation plus its common radical."


The open contract is now:


J_NESTED_PHYSICAL_DUAL_RADICAL_OCCUPANCY:
count the actually realized pairs
(Sigma_xy,Sigma_R)
on S_B^hard13 using genuinely nested physical selector information beyond the macro product triple, while retaining
kappa=rad(G0)>T,
Sigma_xy=kappa A_xy,
Sigma_R=kappa A_R,
gcd(kappa,A_xy A_R)=gcd(A_xy,A_R)=1,
and on J>K,
A_xy A_R>K/3.


The 229CG lambda_i^2 route remains parallel.
If no nested-selector saving is available, return to eta/tau/M_i/K_cross.


Do not retry:
- separate Sigma_xy or Sigma_R tails (229CI firewall);
- macro-Pythagorean joint-pair occupancy using only X^2+Y^2=Z^2, height and common radical (229CJ firewall).


8. State


CURRENT_BLOCKER remains
NO_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_OCCUPIED_SUPPORT_SAVING_FOR_THE_229CC_SIX_BUCKET_COVER_ON_THE_EXACT_HARD13_PHYSICAL_SOURCE.


REFINED_BLOCKER=
NO_ONE_THIRD_COUNT_FOR_LARGE_eta_OR_TAU_FULL_GCD_SQUARE_MODULI_OR_J_NESTED_PHYSICAL_DUAL_RADICAL_OCCUPANCY_OR_MATCHED_DISJOINT_M_U_M_V_M_z.


J_NESTED_PHYSICAL_DUAL_RADICAL_OCCUPANCY=OPEN.
J_OCCUPIED_LAMBDA_SQUARE_MODULUS_SAVING=OPEN.
TAU_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_AMPLIFICATION=OPEN_BUT_FIXED_Q_MECHANISM_RULED_OUT_AT_CONE_LEVEL.
KERNEL_BIAS_BRIDGE=OPEN.


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229 unchanged.
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228 unchanged.
M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.
Existing authority/credit/gate/closure/HOLD states and INTEGRATED_AUDIT_186_229O scope unchanged.
No perfect-cuboid existence/nonexistence conclusion and no new global endpoint exponent are claimed.

records.title: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CI — single-Pythagorean radical occupancy floor and dual-receiver correlation firewall
records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CI — single-Pythagorean radical occupancy floor and dual-receiver correlation firewall
STATUS: POST_229CH_JOINT_RADICAL_PAIR / EXACT_COMMON_RADICAL_DECOMPOSITION / SINGLE_FACE_SIGMA_XY_OCCUPANCY_FLOOR / SINGLE_OUTER_SIGMA_R_OCCUPANCY_FLOOR / SEPARATE_RECEIVER_ATTACK_NO_GO / CROSS_SELECTOR_CORRELATION_REQUIRED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
CARD_DOC_ID=1jfhq7VijeE4xaOykbt6COUrRdmZODywEcaZwJHwhKiA
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CH
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope


Work from 229CH on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) physical source, but audit what can and cannot be obtained from each of its two quadratic radical receivers separately:
Sigma_xy=rad(xy),
Sigma_R=rad(eR),
G0=gcd(eR,xy),
T=B^(1/3-delta).


The aim is not to count endpoints by an ambient family. It is to determine whether a theorem using only one Pythagorean equation, its height, and the fixed-value B^o fiber can possibly deliver the one-third tail.


2. Exact joint radical decomposition


Put
kappa:=rad(G0).                                                (CI.1)


Because gcd(rad(xy),rad(eR))=rad(gcd(xy,eR)),
gcd(Sigma_xy,Sigma_R)=kappa.                                  (CI.2)


Define
A_xy:=Sigma_xy/kappa,
A_R :=Sigma_R/kappa.                                          (CI.3)


Since all three quantities are squarefree,
kappa,A_xy,A_R are pairwise coprime and
Sigma_xy=kappa A_xy,
Sigma_R =kappa A_R.                                           (CI.4)


Retain 229CH:
J_xy|Sigma_xy,
J_e|Sigma_R,
J_xy J_e=J_sharp=J/gcd(J,3),
and gcd(J_sharp,G0)=1.
Therefore exactly
J_xy|A_xy,
J_e |A_R,
J_sharp|A_xy A_R.                                             (CI.5)


On the current source sf(G0)>T, hence kappa>T.
If J>K then
A_xy A_R > K/3.                                               (CI.6)


Also
Sigma_xy Sigma_R
 =kappa^2 A_xy A_R
 <=xy*eR
 =e x y R
 <=R^4/(3 sqrt(3))
 <=B^4/(3 sqrt(3)),                                           (CI.7)
using e^2+x^2+y^2=R^2 and exy<=R^3/(3sqrt3).


RESULT_229CI_EXACT_DUAL_RADICAL_COMMON_FACTOR_DECOMPOSITION=PROVED.
RESULT_229CI_J_SHARP_LIVES_IN_COPRIME_DUAL_RESIDUAL_RADICALS=PROVED_EXACT.


This identifies the genuinely joint object. A theorem that treats Sigma_xy and Sigma_R separately discards (CI.2)-(CI.6).


3. Single missing-face Pythagorean host already has B^(1/2-o(1)) large Sigma_xy values


Let P_xy(B) be the ambient set of positive integer triples
x^2+y^2=z^2,
z<=B.
No other Stage37 selector is imposed in this section.


For large B set
M=floor(sqrt(B)/4).
For every odd prime p in
M<=p<=3M/2,
take
x_p=2p,
y_p=p^2-1,
z_p=p^2+1.                                                    (CI.8)


Then x_p^2+y_p^2=z_p^2 and z_p<B for all sufficiently large B.


Define
s_p=rad(x_p y_p)=rad(2p(p^2-1)).                              (CI.9)


The values s_p are pairwise distinct.
Indeed let p!=q be primes in [M,3M/2].
If q|p^2-1, then q|(p-1)(p+1), so q divides p-1 or p+1.
But 0<p+1<2M<=2q for large M, hence the quotient would have to be 1; this is impossible because p±1 is even and q is odd.
Thus q does not divide 2p(p^2-1).
In particular s_p contains p and does not contain any other prime q from the chosen interval, proving distinctness.


By the prime number theorem,
#{p prime:M<=p<=3M/2} >> M/log M >> B^(1/2)/log B.            (CI.10)


Also
s_p>=p>=M>>B^(1/2).                                           (CI.11)


Therefore
#{Sigma_xy values on P_xy(B) exceeding c B^(1/2)}
 >> B^(1/2)/log B                                             (CI.12)
for an absolute c>0.


RESULT_229CI_SINGLE_MISSING_FACE_SIGMA_XY_OCCUPANCY_FLOOR=B^(1/2-o(1)).


4. Single outer Pythagorean host already has B^(1/2-o(1)) large Sigma_R values


Let P_R(B) be the ambient set of positive integer triples
e^2+z^2=R^2,
R<=B.
Again no other Stage37 selector is imposed.


For every prime p in [M,3M/2], use
e_p=2p,
z_p=p^2-1,
R_p=p^2+1.                                                    (CI.13)


Put
t_p=rad(e_p R_p)=rad(2p(p^2+1)).                              (CI.14)


We extract a large subset with distinct t_p.
Build a graph on the primes in [M,3M/2], joining p!=q if
q|p^2+1 or p|q^2+1.


For fixed p, p^2+1<3M^2 for large M, so it has at most two distinct prime divisors q>=M.
Conversely q^2==-1 mod p has at most two residue classes modulo p, and the interval [M,3M/2] has length <p, so there are at most two q in the interval with p|q^2+1.
Thus the graph has maximum degree at most 4.


A greedy independent set therefore contains at least one fifth of the vertices.
By the prime number theorem it has
>>M/log M>>B^(1/2)/log B                                     (CI.15)
primes.


For distinct p,q in this independent set, q does not divide 2p(p^2+1), so t_p contains p but not q. Hence the t_p are pairwise distinct, and
t_p>=p>=M>>B^(1/2).                                           (CI.16)


Therefore
#{Sigma_R values on P_R(B) exceeding c B^(1/2)}
 >> B^(1/2)/log B.                                            (CI.17)


RESULT_229CI_SINGLE_OUTER_SIGMA_R_OCCUPANCY_FLOOR=B^(1/2-o(1)).


5. Quantitative consequence for the 229CH threshold


The 229CH balanced J threshold is
S_CH=T^(11/10)/(2sqrt3)
    =B^(11/30-(11/10)delta)/(2sqrt3).                         (CI.18)


For every fixed delta>0,
11/30-(11/10)delta < 1/2.
Thus the explicit ambient families in Sections 3-4 lie above S_CH for all sufficiently large B.


Consequently each single Pythagorean host by itself has
>>B^(1/2)/log B
distinct occupied receiver values in the 229CH large-tail range, far above B^(1/3).


Therefore a one-third theorem CANNOT be obtained from either of the following data alone:
- x^2+y^2=z^2, z<=B, Sigma_xy=rad(xy), and fixed-Sigma_xy B^o fiber;
- e^2+z^2=R^2, R<=B, Sigma_R=rad(eR), and fixed-Sigma_R B^o fiber.


RESULT_229CI_SEPARATE_DUAL_RECEIVER_OCCUPIED_TAIL_ATTACK=QUANTITATIVELY_FALSE_ON_THE_SINGLE_PYTHAGOREAN_HOSTS.


Critical scope firewall:
The constructed triples are NOT claimed to be simultaneous Stage37 physical endpoints. Hence (CI.12) and (CI.17) are not lower bounds for the actual endpoint population and do not disprove a selector-aware theorem on the physical intersection.
They prove that any successful continuation must exploit genuinely simultaneous selector/cross-face information.


6. Updated theorem contract


Stop searches for a Sigma_xy tail theorem that uses only the missing-face Pythagorean equation, and stop searches for a Sigma_R tail theorem that uses only the outer Pythagorean equation.


The preferred J theorem input is now:
DUAL_RADICAL_CROSS_SELECTOR_OCCUPANCY:
count the actual same-physical realized pairs
(Sigma_xy,Sigma_R)
on S_B^hard13, retaining
gcd(Sigma_xy,Sigma_R)=kappa=rad(G0)>T,
Sigma_xy=kappa A_xy,
Sigma_R=kappa A_R,
gcd(kappa,A_xy A_R)=gcd(A_xy,A_R)=1,
and on J>K,
A_xy A_R>K/3.


A sufficient form is that the realized pair image in the balanced J branch has
<<B^(1/3-epsilon)
elements for some fixed epsilon>0, since a fixed Sigma_xy value already has physical fiber B^o(1).


Equivalent valid mechanisms may prove a same-physical correlation/dispersion theorem coupling the two Pythagorean completions. The 229CG lambda_i^2 route remains parallel.


CURRENT_BLOCKER remains
NO_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_OCCUPIED_SUPPORT_SAVING_FOR_THE_229CC_SIX_BUCKET_COVER_ON_THE_EXACT_HARD13_PHYSICAL_SOURCE.


REFINED_BLOCKER=
NO_ONE_THIRD_COUNT_FOR_LARGE_eta_OR_TAU_FULL_GCD_SQUARE_MODULI_OR_J_DUAL_RADICAL_CROSS_SELECTOR_OCCUPANCY_OR_MATCHED_DISJOINT_M_U_M_V_M_z.


J_DUAL_QUADRATIC_OCCUPIED_TAIL is superseded as a separate-receiver contract by
J_DUAL_RADICAL_CROSS_SELECTOR_OCCUPANCY=OPEN.
J_OCCUPIED_LAMBDA_SQUARE_MODULUS_SAVING=OPEN.
TAU_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_AMPLIFICATION=OPEN_BUT_FIXED_Q_MECHANISM_RULED_OUT_AT_CONE_LEVEL.
KERNEL_BIAS_BRIDGE=OPEN.


7. State


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229 unchanged.
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228 unchanged.
M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.
Existing authority/credit/gate/closure/HOLD states and INTEGRATED_AUDIT_186_229O scope unchanged.
No perfect-cuboid existence/nonexistence conclusion and no new global endpoint exponent are claimed.
INDEPENDENT_HOSTILE_AUDIT_229CI=NOT_RUN.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CH — dual quadratic radical compression of the J branch
STATUS: POST_229CG_DUAL_QUADRATIC_RADICAL_COMPRESSION / SIGMA_XY_FIXED_FIBER / J_TWO_CHANNEL_SPLIT / BALANCED_J_THRESHOLD_AMPLIFICATION / KXI_PHYSICAL_SIMPLIFICATION / NO_COUNTING_PROMOTION / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
CARD_DOC_ID=1t5O0vzE_GSWYpoUzLotSov9dfY4LueoiPdTbd82ICOI
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CG
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope and notation firewall


Work on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) physical source with all positive primitive Stage37 selectors and R<=B.
Put
T=B^(1/3-delta),
G0=gcd(eR,xy),
so sf(G0)>T on the current source.


To avoid the historical letter collision, in this card write
h_edge:=gcd(e,R)=gcd(g,q)
for the 229AD physical content, and
eta:=rad(Q)
for the 229CC outer-gap conductor bucket formerly also denoted h.


Retain 229CG:
J_sharp:=J/gcd(J,3),
J_sharp|EXY,
gcd(J_sharp,G0)=1,
where
E=g/h_edge, X=c/c21, Y=f/c12,
and the three p>3 J colors satisfy
r_U^#:=r_U/gcd(r_U,3) | Y,
r_V^#:=r_V/gcd(r_V,3) | X,
r_z^#:=r_z/gcd(r_z,3) | E.


2. Two quadratic physical radical receivers


Define
Sigma_xy:=rad(xy),                                           (CH.1)
Sigma_R :=rad(eR).                                           (CH.2)


Both are squarefree and satisfy
Sigma_xy < B^2,
Sigma_R  < B^2.                                              (CH.3)


Sigma_R is the retained 229BR scalar and has uniform fixed-value physical fiber B^o(1).


We now prove the same for Sigma_xy.


Fix a squarefree k=Sigma_xy. Then every prime divisor of x and y lies in supp(k), with x,y<B. By the retained 229BQ uniform prescribed-prime-support lemma, there are B^o(1) possible x values and B^o(1) possible y values, uniformly in k.


For fixed positive (x,y), z is uniquely determined if x^2+y^2 is a square. Also
(U-e)(U+e)=x^2.
Thus the possible positive pairs (e,U) are bounded by tau(x^2)=B^o(1). Each e then determines V and R uniquely if e^2+y^2 and e^2+z^2 are squares. All original selectors only delete candidates.


Hence uniformly
#{P:R<=B, Sigma_xy(P)=k}=B^o(1).                             (CH.4)


RESULT_229CH_SIGMA_XY_QUADRATIC_HEIGHT_FIXED_FIBER_B_O1=PROVED.
RETAINED_229BR_SIGMA_R_QUADRATIC_HEIGHT_FIXED_FIBER_B_O1=true.


3. Split the J support into xy-side and eR-side channels


Define
J_xy:=r_U^# r_V^#,                                           (CH.5)
J_e :=r_z^#.                                                  (CH.6)


By 229CG and pairwise coprimality,
J_xy J_e=J_sharp.                                             (CH.7)


Moreover
J_xy | XY | xy,                                               (CH.8)
because X|x and Y|y, while
J_e | E | e | eR.                                             (CH.9)


Therefore
J_xy | Sigma_xy,
J_e  | Sigma_R.                                               (CH.10)


The current source content also satisfies
G0|xy and G0|eR.
Let
K0_odd:=sf_odd(G0).                                           (CH.11)


Since sf(G0)>T,
K0_odd>T/2.                                                   (CH.12)


By 229CG,
gcd(J_sharp,G0)=1,
hence
gcd(J_xy,K0_odd)=gcd(J_e,K0_odd)=1.                           (CH.13)


Consequently
K0_odd J_xy | Sigma_xy,
K0_odd J_e  | Sigma_R.                                       (CH.14)


RESULT_229CH_J_TWO_CHANNEL_EXACT_DIVISIBILITY=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Deterministic J-large compression to two quadratic tails


If J>K, then
J_sharp=J/gcd(J,3)>K/3.                                      (CH.15)


Using J_sharp=J_xy J_e,
max(J_xy,J_e)>sqrt(K/3).                                     (CH.16)


Combining (CH.12)-(CH.14),
J>K and sf(G0)>T imply
max(Sigma_xy,Sigma_R)
 > (T/2)*sqrt(K/3)
 = T sqrt(K)/(2sqrt(3)).                                      (CH.17)


Thus the whole J-large branch is covered by only two actual physical radical tails, each of quadratic height and each with B^o(1) fixed-value fiber.


At the balanced 229CC cutoff
K=T^(1/5),
(CH.17) becomes
max(Sigma_xy,Sigma_R)

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CG — opposite-difference norm square-modulus lift and J residual-core/cubic-support compression
STATUS: POST_229CF_OPPOSITE_DIFFERENCE_NORM / FULL_LAMBDA_SQUARE_MODULUS / IMPROVED_FIXED_LAMBDA_PACKING / J_SQUARE_GAP_SUPPORT / J_RESIDUAL_CORE_CROSSWALK / CUBIC_KXI_FIXED_FIBER / J_TAIL_STILL_TOO_WEAK / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
CARD_DOC_ID=1AkKIpenTLvLx0-FjW9rTQB4VBZLWIvzntmzhN2UfsLc
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA=Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CF
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope


Work on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) physical source with all positive primitive Stage37 selectors and R<=B.


Retain
A=R-U, Bv=R-V, C=R-z,
S=A+Bv+C,
Omega=ABvC,
ABv+AC+BvC=2d^2,
D=2d,
and 229CF
lambda_U=gcd(A,S)=gcd(A,Bv+C),
lambda_V=gcd(Bv,S)=gcd(Bv,A+C),
lambda_z=gcd(C,S)=gcd(C,A+Bv),
with lambda_U,lambda_V,lambda_z pairwise-coprime odd,
gcd(Omega,S)=lambda_U lambda_V lambda_z,
J=rad(lambda_U)rad(lambda_V)rad(lambda_z).


Retain 229AD/229BN nested physical factorization
e=gab,
x=d0 b c,
y=d0 a f,
h=gcd(g,q),
c12|f,
c21|c,
E=g/h,
X=c/c21,
Y=f/c12,
G0=ab c12 c21,
and
H0=d0^2 X Y,
H1=b^2 E X,
H2=a^2 E Y.


This card strengthens the J router from modulus lambda_i to square modulus lambda_i^2, identifies the p>3 J support inside the residual cores E,X,Y, and compresses the simultaneous large-sf(G0)+large-J branch into one cubic-height fixed-fiber radical scalar.


2. Exact opposite-difference norm identities


Put
u=Bv+C,
t=A+C,
s=A+Bv.


From the cone equation
A u+Bv C=2d^2.
Therefore
(Bv-C)^2+8d^2
 =u^2-4BvC+8d^2
 =u^2+4Au
 =u(u+4A).                                                    (CG.1)


Cyclically,
(A-C)^2+8d^2=t(t+4Bv),                                      (CG.2)
(A-Bv)^2+8d^2=s(s+4C).                                      (CG.3)


These are exact positive-integer factorizations on the same physical source.


RESULT_229CG_OPPOSITE_DIFFERENCE_NORM_FACTORIZATIONS=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Full lambda-square modulus lift


Because lambda_U divides both A and u, (CG.1) gives
lambda_U^2 | (Bv-C)^2+8d^2.                                 (CG.4)


Also
gcd(lambda_U,d)=1.
Indeed if an odd prime p divided lambda_U and d, then p|A and p|u=Bv+C. The cone equation gives Bv C==0 mod p. Since u==0 mod p, this forces p|Bv and p|C, contradicting gcd(A,Bv,C)=1.


Hence 2d is invertible modulo lambda_U^2. Define
sigma_U == (Bv-C)(2d)^(-1) mod lambda_U^2.
Dividing (CG.4) by 4d^2 gives
sigma_U^2 == -2 mod lambda_U^2,                              (CG.5)
and
Bv-C == 2 sigma_U d mod lambda_U^2.                          (CG.6)


Cyclically there are exact roots sigma_V,sigma_z modulo lambda_V^2,lambda_z^2:
A-C == 2 sigma_V d mod lambda_V^2,
A-Bv == 2 sigma_z d mod lambda_z^2,
with sigma_i^2==-2 modulo the corresponding full square modulus.


Thus 229CF's modulo-lambda_i root line is strictly strengthened to a square-modulus root line modulo lambda_i^2, on the opposite-gap difference.


For each lambda_i=m, the number of possible roots sigma mod m^2 is
2^omega(m)=B^o(1)
because every odd prime divisor of m admits -2 and Hensel lifting gives exactly two roots at each prime power.


RESULT_229CG_J_FULL_GCD_SQUARE_MODULUS_ROOT_LINE=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Physical gap-square support and J^2|Omega


Let p|rad(lambda_U)=r_U.
Then p|A and p|S, and by the previous section p does not divide d. Since
R=S+2d,
p does not divide R.


Now
y^2=A(R+U).
Because p|A gives U==R mod p and p does not divide R,
R+U==2R is a p-unit.
Therefore
v_p(A)=2v_p(y),
so v_p(A) is positive even and in particular
p^2|A.


Thus
r_U^2|A.
Cyclically,
r_V^2|Bv,
r_z^2|C.                                                     (CG.7)


Since the r_i are pairwise coprime,
J^2=(r_U r_V r_z)^2 | Omega=ABvC.                            (CG.8)


As A,Bv,C<R<=B,
r_U,r_V,r_z < B^(1/2).                                      (CG.9)


RESULT_229CG_J_MATCHED_RADICALS_SQUARE_DIVIDE_THEIR_OUTER_GAPS=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CG_J_SQUARED_DIVIDES_OMEGA=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Improved fixed-lambda physical packing


Fix lambda_U=m and one root sigma modulo m^2.
Set
Xopp=Bv-C.
Then (CG.6) puts (Xopp,d) in the lattice
Lambda(m,sigma)={(X,Y) in Z^2 : X==2 sigma Y mod m^2}.       (CG.10)


Its determinant is m^2.
For every nonzero vector (X,Y) in this lattice,
m^2 | X^2+8Y^2,
so
X^2+8Y^2 >= m^2.
Therefore the shortest weighted lattice vector has scale at least m, and standard ellipse/lattice packing in
|X|<B, 0<Y<B
gives
#{(Xopp,d) in Lambda(m,sigma)} << 1+B^2/m^2.                 (CG.11)


For fixed (Xopp,d), put
N=Xopp^2+8d^2.
By (CG.1),
N=u(u+4A).
There are at most tau(N)=B^o(1) positive divisor choices for u. Each choice forces
A=(N/u-u)/4,
Bv=(u+Xopp)/2,
C=(u-Xopp)/2.
Integrality, positivity, chamber conditions and the remaining physical square selectors only delete candidates; the retained outer-gap reconstruction gives at most one labelled endpoint from each surviving triple.


Summing the B^o(1) roots,
#{P:R<=B, lambda_U(P)=m}
 << B^o(1)(1+B^2/m^2).                                      (CG.12)


The same estimate holds cyclically.


This strictly supersedes the weaker quantitative bound
B^o(1)(1+B^2/m)
from 229CF. The 229CF full-gcd factorization and all its structural statements remain retained.


RESULT_229CG_FIXED_FULL_OPPOSITE_GCD_SQUARE_MODULUS_PACKING=PROVED.


6. Unrestricted J-large tail remains far too weak


Fix a squarefree r.
The retained 229BQ prescribed-support lemma implies only B^o(1) possible m<=B with rad(m)=r.
Combining with (CG.12),
#{P:R<=B, rad(lambda_i(P))=r}
 << B^o(1)(1+B^2/r^2).                                      (CG.13)


If J>K, one of the three pairwise-coprime radicals r_i exceeds K^(1/3).
By (CG.9), r_i<B^(1/2).
Hence unrestricted summation gives only
#{P:R<=B, J(P)>K}
 << B^(1/2+o(1)) + B^(2+o(1)) K^(-1/3).                     (CG.14)


At the balanced 229CC threshold K=T^(1/5), T=B^(1/3-delta), this is still vastly above B^(1/3).
In particular even the cardinality term from unrestricted radical summation has a B^(1/2+o(1)) floor.


Thus the square-modulus lift is a genuine structural improvement but does not create global counting credit by unrestricted modulus summation.


RESULT_229CG_UNRESTRICTED_J_SQUARE_MODULUS_TAIL_TOO_WEAK=PROVED_QUANTITATIVE_FIREWALL.


7. J support crosswalk into the 229BN residual cores


Retain
e=gab,
x=d0 b c,
y=d0 a f,
E=g/h,
X=c/c21,
Y=f/c12.


We now localize every p>3 in J.


7.1 U-label


Let p>3 divide r_U.
Then p|A and p|Bv+C.
As above p does not divide R and p|y.
Thus p divides one of d0,a,f.


It cannot divide d0:
then p|x,y,z. Since p|A, U==R. Because Bv is a p-unit and x^2=Bv(R+V), p|x forces V==-R. Then
Bv+C=2R-V-z==3R,
contradicting p|Bv+C for p>3.


It cannot divide a:
then p|e,y, so V==0. From Bv+C=2R-V-z==0, z==2R. But R^2=e^2+z^2 and e==0 give 1==4 mod p, forcing p=3.


It cannot divide c12:
c12|U, while p|A=R-U; hence p|R, contradiction.


Therefore p|f but p does not divide c12, so
p|Y=f/c12.
Thus
r_U/gcd(r_U,3) | Y.                                         (CG.15)


7.2 V-label


The cyclic argument gives
r_V/gcd(r_V,3) | X=c/c21.                                   (CG.16)


Explicitly, p|r_V implies p|Bv and p|A+C, hence p|x. For p>3 the possibilities p|d0 and p|b force the same 3R or 4R^2==R^2 contradiction, while p|c21 together with c21|V and Bv=R-V forces p|R.


7.3 z-label


Let p>3 divide r_z.
Then p|C and p|A+Bv, hence p|e.
The possibilities p|a or p|b force, through the two face-square equations and A+Bv=0, the same p=3 contradiction.
Also p cannot divide h: h|e,z, and p|C=R-z would then force p|R.
Therefore p divides g/h=E:
r_z/gcd(r_z,3) | E.                                         (CG.17)


Since E,X,Y are pairwise coprime and r_U,r_V,r_z are pairwise coprime, this is a color-preserving injection of all p>3 J-support into the three residual cores.


Define
J_sharp := J/gcd(J,3).
Then
J_sharp | E X Y.                                             (CG.18)


Moreover the exclusions above, together with c12|f, c21|c, gcd(c,f)=1 and the retained content coprimalities, give
gcd(J_sharp,G0)=1,
where
G0=ab c12 c21.                                               (CG.19)


RESULT_229CG_J_ODD_GT3_SUPPORT_COLOR_INJECTS_INTO_Y_X_E=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CG_J_SHARP_DIVIDES_EXY_AND_IS_COPRIME_TO_G0=PROVED_EXACT.


8. Cubic one-scalar receiver for simultaneous large sf(G0) and large J


Define
K_Xi := rad(G0 H0 H1 H2).                                    (CG.20)


Retain 229BN
H0H1H2=(a b d0 E X Y)^2.
Therefore exactly
K_Xi=rad(G0 d0 E X Y).                                      (CG.21)


Using
G0=ab c12 c21,
E=g/h,
X=c/c21,
Y=f/c12,
we have
G0 d0 E X Y
 = d0 (e/h) c f.                                             (CG.22)


The primitive missing-face equation gives
q^2=(bc)^2+(af)^2 >= 2abcf,
and z=d0 q.
Hence
d0(e/h)cf
 <= e z^2/(2 h a b d0).                                     (CG.23)


Under e^2+z^2=R^2,
e z^2 <= 2R^3/(3 sqrt(3)).
Thus
K_Xi
 <= R^3/(3 sqrt(3) h a b d0)
 <= B^3/(3 sqrt(3)).                                         (CG.24)


So K_Xi has genuine cubic physical height.


Fixed-value fiber:
for fixed squarefree k=K_Xi, each of G0,H0,H1,H2 is <=B^2 and has all prime divisors in supp(k). The retained 229BQ uniform prescribed-prime-support/Rankin lemma gives only B^o(1) possible values for each coordinate. For each fixed quadruple Xi=(G0,H0,H1,H2), 229BN gives B^o(1) physical endpoints. Therefore uniformly
#{P:R<=B, K_Xi(P)=k}=B^o(1).                                (CG.25)


Now combine the current preferred large-radical source with (CG.18)-(CG.19).
Since sf(G0) and J_sharp are coprime and both divide K_Xi,
sf(G0) J_sharp | K_Xi.                                      (CG.26)


On the exact current source,
sf(G0)>T.
On a J-large branch J>K,
J_sharp> K/3.
Therefore
K_Xi > T K/3.                                                (CG.27)


In particular on the balanced 229CC J branch
J>T^(1/5),
one has the deterministic compression
K_Xi > (1/3) T^(6/5).                                       (CG.28)


RESULT_229CG_CUBIC_KXI_RECEIVER_FIXED_FIBER_B_O1=PROVED.
RESULT_229CG_LARGE_SF_G0_AND_LARGE_J_FORCE_KXI_GT_TK_OVER3=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CG_BALANCED_J_BRANCH_COMPRESSES_TO_KXI_GT_T_6_OVER5_OVER3=PROVED_EXACT.


This is a new same-physical one-scalar target, not a tail theorem.


9. Quantitative and independence firewalls


The following are NOT proved:
- no occupied-value estimate for large K_Xi;
- no selector-aware saving for the family of lambda_i^2 moduli;
- no one-third count for the J branch;
- no new independence between K_Xi and the other 229CC buckets.


Cubic height plus B^o fixed fiber does not imply a power-saving occupied-value count.
Likewise (CG.14) shows that unrestricted square-modulus summation remains far too weak.


The openai/math common-base and sparse-incidence obstructions from 229CE remain. The 229CF fixed-Q firewall also remains.


10. Updated research contract


For the J branch, replace the weaker 229CF quantitative router by the two new exact interfaces:
(A) lambda_U^2,lambda_V^2,lambda_z^2 opposite-difference -2 root lines with fixed-lambda count B^o(1)(1+B^2/lambda^2);
(B) K_Xi=rad(G0H0H1H2), cubic height, fixed K_Xi fiber B^o, and on J>K the lower bound K_Xi>TK/3.


Highest-value next theorem is one of:
1. SELECTOR_AWARE_OCCUPIED_LAMBDA_SQUARE_MODULUS_SAVING:

2. SELECTOR_AWARE_KXI_OCCUPIED_TAIL:
prove a fixed-power occupied-value/tail bound for the actual K_Xi values realized by S_B^hard13, especially above T^(6/5)/3 on the balanced J branch;
3. if neither is accessible, return to direct K_cross or the remaining h/tau/M_i branches.


For tau, TAU_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_AMPLIFICATION remains open, with the 229CF rule that fixing Q alone is not the common-base mechanism.


Do not infer saving from:
- split-prime support alone;
- J^2|Omega alone;
- cubic height plus fixed K_Xi fiber alone;
- unrestricted lambda/radical modulus summation.


11. Verification and state


Algebraic replay over 4854 positive cone fixtures with A,Bv,C<120, gcd(A,Bv,C)=1, exactly two even gaps and integral d satisfying ABv+AC+BvC=2d^2 checked (CG.1)-(CG.6), gcd(lambda_i,d)=1 and lambda_i^2 divisibility in all three labels with zero failures.
These are cone-lemma fixtures only, not perfect-cuboid endpoints or endpoint-density evidence.


The residual-core crosswalk is proved directly from the exact physical square equations and retained 229AD/229BN content divisibility/coprimality relations; no finite endpoint enumeration is claimed for it.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229CF — full opposite-gcd factorization, J root-line router, and fixed-Q tau common-base firewall
STATUS: POST_229CE_FIXED_Q_COMMON_BASE_FIREWALL / FULL_OPPOSITE_GCD_PRODUCT / EXACT_J_FULL_GCD_RECEIVER / J_MINUS2_ROOT_LINES / FIXED_LAMBDA_PACKING_TOO_WEAK / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN

Work on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) physical source, retaining all positive primitive Stage37 selectors and R<=B.
Retain
A=R-U, Bv=R-V, C=R-z,
S=A+Bv+C,
Omega=ABvC,
ABv+AC+BvC=2d^2,
D=2d,
and the 229CC six-bucket cover.
Retain 229BX's exact desaturated cone and 229CB's tau full-pair-gcd router.


This card does two things:
(i) test whether fixing the 229BX overlap conductor Q can itself create the common fixed base required by the 229CE tau-collision bridge;
(ii) lift the 229CC radical receiver J to an exact full-gcd factorization and derive a new full-prime-power -2 root-line router.


2. Fixed-Q cone family: Q does not freeze the tau modulus


For every integer n>=1 define
A=2n^2-1,
Bv=2,
C=2,
d=2n,
D=4n.                                                     (CF.1)


Then A is odd and Bv,C are even, so the retained parity pattern holds.
Moreover
ABv+AC+BvC
=2A+2A+4
=4(2n^2-1)+4
=8n^2
=2d^2,                                                     (CF.2)
hence
D^2=2(ABv+AC+BvC)
and the exact 229BX outer-gap cone is satisfied.


All odd pairwise gcds of A,Bv,C are 1. Therefore
q_UV=q_Uz=q_Vz=1,
Q=1,                                                        (CF.3)
so this is one fixed-Q desaturated-cone family.


Put
s=A+Bv,
t=A+C,
u=Bv+C.
Then exactly
s=t=2n^2+1,
u=4,
g_A=gcd(s,t)=2n^2+1,
g_B=gcd(s,u)=1,
g_C=gcd(t,u)=1.                                             (CF.4)


Also
H_A=A^2+2d^2=(2n^2+1)^2=g_A^2.                              (CF.5)


Hence even with Q fixed identically to 1, the full tau modulus g_A is unbounded and varies with n.
RESULT_229CF_FIXED_Q_DESATURATED_CONE_DOES_NOT_FREEZE_TAU_MODULUS=PROVED_EXACT.


Firewall:
This is an exact 229BX cone family, not a family of verified perfect-cuboid physical endpoints. Therefore it proves only that the 229BX cone/Q data by themselves do not provide the Problem337-style fixed-base nesting. It does NOT prove that the additional physical square-edge selectors can never create such a common base.


Consequently any proof of
TAU_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_AMPLIFICATION
must use genuinely additional selector information beyond “fix Q / fix the Q-factorization / take a dyadic Q-block”.


3. Full opposite-gcd factorization


Define
lambda_U := gcd(A,S)=gcd(A,Bv+C),
lambda_V := gcd(Bv,S)=gcd(Bv,A+C),
lambda_z := gcd(C,S)=gcd(C,A+Bv).                            (CF.6)


Because exactly two of A,Bv,C are even, S is odd. Therefore all three lambda_i are odd.


They are pairwise coprime.
For example, if a prime p divided lambda_U and lambda_V, then
p|A, p|Bv, p|S,
hence p|C=S-A-Bv, contradicting gcd(A,Bv,C)=1.
The other pairs are cyclic.


Now let
L_J := gcd(Omega,S)=gcd(ABvC,S).                             (CF.7)


Any prime p|L_J divides S and at least one gap.
It cannot divide two gaps: if p|A and p|Bv, then p|S would force p|C, again contradicting gcd(A,Bv,C)=1.
Thus p divides exactly one gap, and its full p-adic valuation in gcd(Omega,S) is exactly the p-adic valuation of the corresponding lambda_i.
Therefore
L_J=lambda_U lambda_V lambda_z                             (CF.8)
as an equality of full positive integers, not merely radicals.


Since 229CC defined
J=rad_odd(gcd(Omega,S)),
and L_J is odd,
J=rad(lambda_U) rad(lambda_V) rad(lambda_z).                (CF.9)


Moreover the three radicals in (CF.9) are pairwise coprime and are exactly the previously defined matched overlap radicals
r_U=rad(lambda_U),
r_V=rad(lambda_V),
r_z=rad(lambda_z).                                          (CF.10)


RESULT_229CF_EXACT_FULL_J_GCD_FACTORIZATION=PROVED.
This strictly strengthens 229CC's scalar radical identity J=rad_odd(gcd(Omega,S)).


4. Exact -2 root lines modulo the full opposite gcds


Consider lambda_U.
Modulo lambda_U,
A=0,
Bv+C=0.
Using
A(Bv+C)+Bv C=2d^2,
we obtain
Bv C == 2d^2 mod lambda_U,
and C==-Bv, hence
Bv^2+2d^2 == 0 mod lambda_U.                                (CF.11)


Also
gcd(lambda_U,Bv d)=1.
Indeed if p|lambda_U and p|Bv, then p|A,Bv,S and hence p|C, impossible.
If p|lambda_U and p|d, then (CF.11) forces p|Bv, again impossible.


Therefore there is a unique residue
rho_U == Bv*d^(-1) mod lambda_U
for the endpoint, satisfying
rho_U^2 == -2 mod lambda_U,
and
Bv == rho_U d mod lambda_U.                                 (CF.12)


Cyclically, after choosing one of the two gaps opposite the lambda-gap,
there are exact root lines modulo lambda_V and lambda_z as well.


For every prime power p^e||lambda_i, -2 is a nonzero quadratic residue modulo p, hence Hensel lifting gives exactly two roots modulo p^e.
By CRT,
#{rho mod lambda_i : rho^2==-2 mod lambda_i}
=2^omega(lambda_i)
=B^o(1),                                                     (CF.13)
uniformly because lambda_i<S<B.


In particular every odd prime p|J satisfies
(-2/p)=1.                                                     (CF.14)


RESULT_229CF_J_FULL_GCD_MINUS2_ROOT_LINE_ROUTER=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229CF_ALL_J_PRIMES_SPLIT_FOR_MINUS2=PROVED.


5. Fixed-lambda physical packing


Fix lambda_U=m and one root rho^2==-2 mod m.
Every physical endpoint in this fiber gives
Bv == rho d mod m,
with 0<Bv<B and 0<d<B.


The lattice
Lambda(m,rho)={(X,Y) in Z^2 : X==rho Y mod m}
has the property that every nonzero vector satisfies
m | X^2+2Y^2.
Hence its weighted norm is at least sqrt(m), and standard ellipse packing gives
#{(X,Y) in Lambda(m,rho):0<X,Y<B}
<< 1+B^2/m.                                                   (CF.15)


For a fixed pair (Bv,d),
H_B=Bv^2+2d^2=(A+Bv)(Bv+C)                                  (CF.16)
is fixed.
There are at most tau(H_B)=B^o(1) ordered positive factor pairs
(s,u)=(A+Bv,Bv+C).
Each such pair forces
A=s-Bv,
C=u-Bv,
and 229BU reconstruction gives at most one positive physical endpoint.


Summing the 2^omega(m)=B^o(1) roots,
#{P:R<=B, lambda_U(P)=m}
<< B^o(1)(1+B^2/m).                                          (CF.17)


The same estimate holds cyclically for lambda_V and lambda_z.
RESULT_229CF_FIXED_FULL_OPPOSITE_GCD_PHYSICAL_PACKING=PROVED.


6. J-large consequence and quantitative firewall


Since
J=rad(lambda_U)rad(lambda_V)rad(lambda_z)
with pairwise-coprime factors, if J>K then at least one lambda_i satisfies
rad(lambda_i)>K^(1/3),
hence
lambda_i>K^(1/3).                                            (CF.18)


However unrestricted summation of (CF.17) over m>M gives only
B^o(1) sum_{M<m<B}(1+B^2/m)
<< B^(1+o(1)) + B^(2+o(1)) log(B/M),                         (CF.19)
which has no useful one-third saving at the current thresholds.


Thus the new J router is structurally exact but quantitatively insufficient by naive modulus summation.
It is weaker in modulus power than the 229CB tau square-modulus router, so it must not be promoted to a counting result without additional occupied-modulus or selector correlation.


RESULT_229CF_J_ROOT_LINE_PACKING_ALONE_TOO_WEAK=PROVED_QUANTITATIVE_FIREWALL.


7. External-adapter implications


The 229CE tau conclusion is sharpened:
fixing Q, its factorization, or a Q-block cannot by itself be the missing common fixed base, because the exact family (CF.1)-(CF.5) has Q=1 while g_A varies unboundedly.
A surviving tau collision route must use selector data not encoded merely by the 229BX cone/Q coordinates.


The J conclusion is also sharpened:
J now has an exact full-gcd modulus decomposition and unary -2 root lines modulo lambda_i, so a future direct occupied-lambda theorem can bypass the earlier radical-only representation.
Nevertheless this does not solve the 229CE sparse matched-incidence problem and does not create a Problem337 common base.


The kernel-bias route is not activated by (CF.14).
The openai/math quadratic_biased_kernel_count / eventual_affine_kernel_count hypotheses require a common prime set P and a uniform lower bound for a quadraticPrimeMean across every kernel in the counted set.
The fact that the prime divisors of one endpoint's J individually satisfy (-2/p)=1 is a support-local splitting condition, not such a shared-prime character-mean hypothesis.
KERNEL_BIAS_BRIDGE remains OPEN.


8. Updated research contract


Current preferred exact receivers now include
tau: 229CB full pair-gcd square-modulus router,
J: 229CF full opposite-gcd factorization and full-modulus -2 root-line router,
plus the 229CC six-bucket decomposition and K_cross receiver.


For TAU_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_AMPLIFICATION:
do not retry “fix Q”, “fix Q factorization”, or “dyadic Q block” as the common-base mechanism. Any further attempt must explicitly use additional physical square-edge/selective data and show why all bad/realized q in a block act on one common pool.


For J:
the next useful target is a selector-aware occupied-lambda theorem for
lambda_U=lambda gcd(A,S), lambda_V=gcd(Bv,S), lambda_z=gcd(C,S),
or a bounded-fiber encoding that turns the new full-gcd router into a genuine sparse-incidence/bilinear saving.


Direct occupied-tail control for
K_cross=rad_odd(Omega*Pi)
remains an alternative.


Do not infer a global saving from split-prime support, fixed-lambda packing, or unrestricted summation of root-line moduli.


9. State


CURRENT_BLOCKER remains
NO_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_OCCUPIED_SUPPORT_SAVING_FOR_THE_229CC_SIX_BUCKET_COVER_ON_THE_EXACT_HARD13_PHYSICAL_SOURCE.


REFINED_BLOCKER remains
NO_ONE_THIRD_COUNT_FOR_LARGE_h_OR_TAU_FULL_GCD_SQUARE_MODULI_OR_J_FULL_OPPOSITE_GCD_MODULI_OR_MATCHED_DISJOINT_M_U_M_V_M_z.


TAU_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_AMPLIFICATION=OPEN_BUT_FIXED_Q_MECHANISM_RULED_OUT_AT_CONE_LEVEL.
J_SPARSE_MATCHED_INCIDENCE_BILINEARIZATION=OPEN.
J_OCCUPIED_FULL_GCD_MODULUS_SAVING=OPEN.
KERNEL_BIAS_BRIDGE=OPEN.


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229 unchanged.
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228 unchanged.
M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.
Existing authority/credit/gate/closure/HOLD states and INTEGRATED_AUDIT_186_229O scope unchanged.
No perfect-cuboid existence/nonexistence conclusion and no new global endpoint exponent are claimed.
INDEPENDENT_HOSTILE_AUDIT_229CF=NOT_RUN.
SANITY_REPLAY_229CF=3369 parity/cone fixtures with A,Bv,C<100, gcd(A,Bv,C)=1, integral d: full factorization, pairwise coprimality, radical identity, and root congruences all passed; these are lemma fixtures only.

STATUS: POST_229CD_ADAPTER_EXECUTION_AUDIT / TAU_COMMON_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_OBSTRUCTION / J_SPARSE_MATCHED_INCIDENCE_BILINEAR_OBSTRUCTION / NO_DIRECT_EXTERNAL_TRANSFER / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN

Execute the two leading 229CD external adapters against the exact Stage37 hosts rather than only classifying theorem names.

g_A=gcd(s,t), g_B=gcd(s,u), g_C=gcd(t,u),
rad(g_Ag_Bg_C)=tau,
g_A^2|A^2+2d^2 cyclically,

plus the cyclic analogues.


External source remains
openai/math@adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a.


2. Tau collision adapter — exact host test


Relevant source:
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/EgyptianFractions/CollisionCounting.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/EgyptianFractions/RoughModulusCollision.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/EgyptianFractions/RoughModulusBlocks.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/EgyptianFractions/CompositeBadModuli.lean


The generic collision theorems require one common finite domain A for all moduli/maps under consideration.
For a modulus q, the hypothesis is a high collision energy or equivalently a sufficiently small image of that same common A.
The off-diagonal double count then uses the fact that any fixed distinct pair of elements of A can collide for only restrictedly many moduli.


The block implementation in RoughModulusBlocks is explicit about this structure: all bad moduli in a dyadic block are tested against one fixed divisor list. CompositeBadModuli first transfers the q-dependent badness to that fixed base and only then performs the collision double count.


229CB supplies a different type of datum. For a physical endpoint P with g_A(P)=m it supplies the unary membership
(A(P),d(P)) lies on one of the 2^omega(m) root lines modulo m^2.
Equivalently, for the q-dependent fiber
E_q={P:q=m(P)^2 in the relevant A-router},
the slope/root image is small on E_q.


This does not imply a small image or high collision energy on one common endpoint set E independent of q.
If one defines E_q and uses the root-line pigeonhole inside E_q, the domain itself changes with q, so exceptional_maps_card_le / moduli_rpow_energy_card_le cannot be invoked.
If one instead takes one global E, 229CB guarantees only that the endpoint(s) realizing q lie in the root set; it gives no lower bound saying a positive q-dependent fraction of all E lies in that root set. Hence the required collision-energy inequality is not discharged.


RESULT_229CE_TAU_ROOT_LINE_TO_COMMON_COLLISION_DIRECT_TRANSFER=FAILS_AT_COMMON_DOMAIN_HYPOTHESIS.
This is a host-implication failure, not a theorem that no additional Stage37 structure could ever create the needed common base.


Precise missing theorem:
TAU_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_AMPLIFICATION=
for each relevant dyadic modulus block, construct one selector-exact finite common pool A_D independent of q and prove that every realized/bad q in that block inherits high residue/projective-slope collision energy on A_D, with an off-diagonal restricted-modulus multiplicity B^o(1), while preserving the physical endpoint-to-q accounting at R<=B.


Without this amplification/nesting step, Problem337 collision machinery cannot count the 229CB occupied tau moduli.


3. J large-gcd adapter — exact host test


Relevant source:
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveLargeGcd.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveLargeGcdBasic.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveLargeGcdBound.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveGcdSeparation.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveGcdSeparationBound.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveGcdSeparationSelection.lean


The symmetric weighted_large_gcd_removal decomposes a Jacobi quadratic energy over one common odd-squarefree column set by gcd(n,t)=d and bounds the large-d tail through shorter quotient support.


The repository also contains genuinely bilinear two-column-set machinery: coprime_jacobi_bilinear_moebius, coprimeDivisorJacobiRow, and exists_gcd_separation_scales. Thus the earlier 229CD audit is sharpened: the absence of two different column sets is NOT the obstruction.


The remaining mismatch is sparse matched incidence.


Stage37 has, endpoint by endpoint,
r_U(P)=gcd(u_U(P),w_u(P)),
r_V(P)=gcd(u_V(P),w_t(P)),
r_z(P)=gcd(u_z(P),w_s(P)),
and
J(P)=r_U(P)r_V(P)r_z(P)=rad_odd(gcd(Omega(P),S(P))).


A large J therefore yields a large gcd on at least one matched edge
(u_i(P),w_i(P))
after a three-label pigeonhole.


Across endpoints, however, these matched pairs form a sparse incidence set
E_i subset U_i x W_i.
The Ostmann bilinear forms sum over Cartesian products S x T with factorable coefficient weights a(n)b(t), together with arithmetic coprimality/divisibility conditions. They do not accept an arbitrary incidence indicator 1_{(n,t) in E_i} as a host input.


Replacing the Stage37 matched-edge sum by the full Cartesian U_i x W_i creates cross-endpoint pairs not present in the physical source and does not preserve the desired lower bound/counting direction. Arbitrary decomposition of the incidence matrix into product weights has no proved subpower complexity bound.


RESULT_229CE_J_MATCHED_GCD_TO_OSTMANN_DIRECT_TRANSFER=FAILS_AT_SPARSE_INCIDENCE_FACTORIZATION_HYPOTHESIS.


Precise missing theorem:
J_SPARSE_MATCHED_INCIDENCE_BILINEARIZATION=
either
(a) prove that the selector-conditioned Stage37 matched incidence matrix for one label has B^o(1) factorization/biclique complexity compatible with Ostmann's bilinear gcd/Jacobi bounds,
or
(b) prove a sparse-graph extension of the relevant large-gcd removal estimate with the same quotient-support saving,
or
(c) construct a different injective/bounded-fiber encoding of J-large endpoints into a genuine common Cartesian/Jacobi energy for which cross terms are harmless and the R-height measure is retained.


The existence of bilinear GcdSeparation modules removes the weaker “only symmetric energy exists” concern, but it does not solve the matched-edge host.


4. Kernel-bias adapter


No new common-prime quadratic-character bias or affine-kernel identification arises from the execution audit.
KERNEL_BIAS_BRIDGE remains OPEN and reserve priority only.


5. Updated external verdict


RESULT_229CE_NO_CURRENT_OPENAI_MATH_ADAPTER_IS_DIRECTLY_EXECUTABLE_FROM_229CC_229CB_DATA=ESTABLISHED_AS_HOST_AUDIT.


This does not retract 229CD's statement that reusable machinery exists.
It refines the bridges:

 -> TAU_FIXED_BASE_COLLISION_AMPLIFICATION.

The tau collision path is no longer preferred merely from the existing root-line data; it becomes actionable only after a fixed-base nesting/amplification theorem.
The J path is likewise actionable only after a matched-incidence bilinearization theorem.

Preferred next work is now one of:

1. Scope and current target


Work on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) physical source, with all positive primitive Stage37 selectors and R<=B retained.
Retain 229CC:
T=B^(1/3-delta),
the six pairwise-coprime odd squarefree support buckets
h, tau, J, M_U, M_V, M_z,
K_cross=h*tau*J*M_U*M_V*M_z=rad_odd(Omega*Pi),
and the deterministic balanced cover
h>T^(1/5)
OR tau>T^(1/5)
OR J>T^(1/5)
OR max(M_U,M_V,M_z)>2^(-3/2)T^(1/5).


No branch above has a one-third endpoint count. The current task is therefore not another algebraic decomposition; it is to locate a selector-aware theorem input capable of counting one branch or the occupied K_cross tail.


2. External source fixed for this audit


SOURCE_REPO=openai/math
SOURCE_COMMIT=adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a


The repository was searched across Lean modules and the associated manuscript sources for:
large sieve, quadratic sieve, large gcd, gcd mass, squarefree kernel, affine kernel, collision energy, square modulus/root models, divisor support, and related terms.


The closest reusable inputs are recorded below. This card does not treat theorem names as sufficient evidence: the exact host hypotheses were checked before classification.


3. Candidate A — Ostmann weighted large-gcd removal


SOURCE_PATHS:
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveLargeGcd.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveLargeGcdBound.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieveLargeGcdBasic.lean


The theorem weighted_large_gcd_removal is an exact large-gcd descent for a weighted Jacobi-character energy. In compressed form, for odd-squarefree columns S<=N, nonnegative row weights omega, and coefficients a, it bounds


weightedNumeratorEnergy(W,S,omega,a)


by


sum_{d<=D} ||weightedGcdCorrelation(W,S,omega,a,d)||
+
C N^epsilon weightedNumeratorNorm(W, oddSquarefreeUpTo(N/D), omega)
  * coefficientEnergy(S,a).


The proof genuinely separates gcd strata and sends the d>D tail to a shorter quotient-support norm. It is not a heuristic density statement.


CLASSIFICATION_229CD_A=ADAPTER_NOT_DIRECT.


Reason for no direct transfer:
Stage37 currently has endpoint multiplicities and the scalar support condition
J=rad_odd(gcd(Omega,S)),
but no proved map from the exact physical endpoint source to a Jacobi matrix whose weightedNumeratorEnergy is bounded below by the J-large endpoint population and whose gcd stratum d is exactly, or boundedly-fibered by, the Stage37 J receiver. The theorem controls an analytic energy after such a matrix has been constructed; it does not itself count arbitrary pairs with large gcd radical.


Required bridge:
J_ENERGY_BRIDGE=
construct, on the exact selector source, odd-squarefree columns n(P), row parameters m, nonnegative weights omega, and coefficients a such that
(i) J-large endpoints force a quantitative lower bound for weightedNumeratorEnergy,
(ii) the relevant gcd strata encode J or a bounded-multiplicity divisor of J,
(iii) the quotient-support norm at N/D is controlled in the same R-height/selector measure,
(iv) all losses are o(B^(1/3)) at a threshold comparable to the 229CC branch threshold.


Without this bridge, importing weighted_large_gcd_removal does not create global counting credit.


4. Candidate B — quadratic large sieve and biased squarefree-kernel count


SOURCE_PATHS:
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/QuadraticSieve/PublishedQuadraticSieve.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/Quadratic/QuadraticKernelCount.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/Characters/AffineKernelCount.lean
lean/OAI/NumberTheory/Ostmann/Quadratic/QuadraticKernelDecomposition.lean
preprints/the-additive-indecomposability-of-the-primes-September-24-2026/build/sections/03-quadratic.tex


PublishedQuadraticLargeSieve is the finite odd-squarefree Heath-Brown quadratic-large-sieve input retained explicitly by the repository.
quadratic_biased_kernel_count converts a common amplified quadratic-character bias into a quantitative bound on the number of signed squarefree kernels.
eventual_affine_kernel_count upgrades this to actual affine values m*x-h: under a strong common-prime bias and scale hypotheses, the number of distinct biased squarefree kernels is exp(o(L)) in the manuscript regime.


This machinery would be very strong if one of the Stage37 support buckets were already a squarefree kernel of a controlled affine value and carried the required common-prime character bias.


CLASSIFICATION_229CD_B=ADAPTER_WITH_MISSING_BIAS_AND_HOST_IDENTIFICATION.


Current firewall:
J is the odd radical of a gcd, not the squarefree kernel of one affine value.

1. Scope
Work on the exact current S_B^hard13(delta) source, retaining all positive primitive Stage37 selectors, exact physical height R<=B, and the corrected229BZ/229CA notation:
A=R-U, Bv=R-V, C=R-z, D=2d>0,
ABv+AC+BvC=2d^2,
s=A+Bv, t=A+C, u=Bv+C,
H_A=st=A^2+2d^2, H_B=su=Bv^2+2d^2, H_C=tu=C^2+2d^2.
Retain229CA's conductor-aligned atoms and its three macro branches. This card does not claim that any branch is counted to one-third scale.


2. Single pair-sum product receiver
Define
Pi(P):=s t u=(A+Bv)(A+C)(Bv+C).                              (CB.1)
Let S=A+Bv+C. Since s+t+u=2S and S<R, AM-GM gives
0<Pi< (2S/3)^3 < 8R^3/27 <= 8B^3/27.                         (CB.2)
Also
(A+Bv)(A+C)(Bv+C)
 = S(ABv+AC+BvC)-ABvC
 = 2S d^2 - Omega,                                             (CB.3)
where Omega=ABvC is the retained229BU outer-gap product. Thus
Pi+Omega=2S d^2,  S=R-2d.                                    (CB.4)
This is an exact additive coupling between the outer-gap product and the pair-sum product.


Fix n=Pi. There are at most d_3(n)=B^o(1) ordered positive triples (s,t,u) with stu=n. Each such triple determines
A=(s+t-u)/2,
Bv=(s+u-t)/2,
C=(t+u-s)/2.                                                   (CB.5)
Nonintegral or nonpositive triples are discarded. For every surviving labelled (A,Bv,C),229BU reconstructs at most one physical endpoint. Hence uniformly for n<=8B^3/27,
#{P:R<=B,Pi(P)=n}<=B^o(1).                                    (CB.6)
RESULT_229CB_FIXED_PAIR_SUM_PRODUCT_PHYSICAL_FIBER_B_O1=PROVED.


Define
k_sum(P):=rad(Pi(P)).                                          (CB.7)
For fixed squarefree k,229BQ's uniform polynomial-height prescribed-prime-support lemma gives only B^o(1) possible Pi values of height O(B^3) with radical k. Combining with (CB.6),
#{P:R<=B,k_sum(P)=k}<=B^o(1).                                 (CB.8)
RESULT_229CB_FIXED_PAIR_SUM_PRODUCT_RADICAL_FIBER_B_O1=PROVED.


By229BZ and229CA,
k_sum=tau*v_s*v_t*v_u
     =2*tau*h*w_s*w_t*w_u.                                    (CB.9)
Thus k_sum is a single exact support receiver for the entire pair-sum side.
Its low sector gives
#{P:R<=B,k_sum<=T}<<T B^o(1),                                 (CB.10)
but on hard13 this is NOT a new disposal: each k_A=rad(st),k_B=rad(su),k_C=rad(tu) divides k_sum, so k_sum<=T is already contained in the retained229BY low-k13 complement.


3. Full pair-gcd lift of tau
Define the full pair gcds
g_A:=gcd(s,t),
g_B:=gcd(s,u),
g_C:=gcd(t,u).                                                  (CB.11)
Since gcd(s,t,u)=1 by229BZ, g_A,g_B,g_C are pairwise coprime. Exactly one of s,t,u is even, hence all three pair gcds are odd.
Put
G:=g_A g_B g_C.                                                 (CB.12)
The common radical atom of229BZ is exactly
rad(G)=tau.                                                     (CB.13)
Moreover
g_A^2 | st=H_A,
g_B^2 | su=H_B,
g_C^2 | tu=H_C,                                                (CB.14)
so
G^2 | Pi.                                                       (CB.15)
Since229CA gives Q^2|Pi and229BZ gives gcd(tau,Q)=1, hence gcd(G,Q)=1, we obtain
(QG)^2 | Pi.                                                    (CB.16)
Also229BX gives Q|D; Q is odd and D=2d, hence
Q|d.                                                           (CB.17)


4. Exact tau square-modulus root lines
Every prime p|tau is coprime to 2dABC and satisfies (-2/p)=1 by229BZ. Therefore
gcd(g_A,Ad)=gcd(g_B,Bv*d)=gcd(g_C,Cd)=1.                       (CB.18)
From (CB.14),
A^2+2d^2==0 mod g_A^2,
Bv^2+2d^2==0 mod g_B^2,
C^2+2d^2==0 mod g_C^2.                                        (CB.19)
Thus there exist unique root choices modulo the corresponding square moduli:
A == rho_A d mod g_A^2,   rho_A^2==-2 mod g_A^2,
Bv== rho_B d mod g_B^2,   rho_B^2==-2 mod g_B^2,
C == rho_C d mod g_C^2,   rho_C^2==-2 mod g_C^2.               (CB.20)
For an odd m all of whose prime divisors split for -2, the congruence rho^2==-2 mod m^2 has exactly 2^omega(m) roots by Hensel lifting and CRT. Since m<B, this multiplicity is B^o(1).
RESULT_229CB_TAU_FULL_PAIR_GCD_SQUARE_MODULUS_ROUTER=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Uniform root-line packing
Fix an odd m and one root rho^2==-2 mod m^2. Consider
Lambda(m,rho)={(X,Y) in Z^2 : X==rho Y mod m^2}.               (CB.21)
For every nonzero lattice vector,
m^2 | X^2+2Y^2,
hence X^2+2Y^2>=m^2.                                          (CB.22)
Therefore distinct lattice points have separation at least m in the weighted norm sqrt(X^2+2Y^2). A disjoint-ellipse packing argument in 0<X,Y<B gives
#{(X,Y) in Lambda(m,rho):0<X,Y<B}
 << 1+B^2/m^2.                                                 (CB.23)
Summing over the 2^omega(m)=B^o(1) admissible roots,
#{(X,Y):0<X,Y<B, m^2|X^2+2Y^2, gcd(m,XY)=1}
 << B^o(1)(1+B^2/m^2).                                        (CB.24)


Apply this to g_A=m and (X,Y)=(A,d). For each (A,d), H_A=A^2+2d^2 is fixed; there are at most d(H_A)=B^o(1) factor pairs st=H_A, after which Bv=s-A and C=t-A are forced and229BU gives at most one physical endpoint. Consequently
#{P:R<=B, g_A(P)=m}
 << B^o(1)(1+B^2/m^2),                                        (CB.25)
uniformly in m. The same bound holds cyclically for g_B and g_C.
RESULT_229CB_FIXED_PAIR_GCD_SQUARE_MODULUS_PACKING=PROVED.


6. Tau-large branch consequence and quantitative firewall

2. Exact conductor-to-pair-sum support crosswalk
Let p|q_UV. Then p|A and p|Bv. Since gcd(A,Bv,C)=1, p does not divide C. Therefore
p|s=A+Bv,
p does not divide t=A+C,
p does not divide u=Bv+C.

Cyclically,

Retain 229BY Sections 2–4: the three H_j identities, the uniform B^o(1) fixed-H_j physical fibers, the uniform B^o(1) fixed-rad(H_j) physical fibers, and the low-radical hard13 reduction.
This card retracts only the 229BY Section 5 inference that H_A H_B H_C being a square forces rad(H_A)rad(H_B)rad(H_C) to be a square or forbids a common radical atom.


2. Exact diagnosis of the 229BY radical inference
The exact identity
H_A H_B H_C=(stu)^2
is retained.
However, radical does not record valuation parity. Therefore the implication
H_AH_BH_C square => rad(H_A)rad(H_B)rad(H_C) square
is false in general.
A parity-compatible primitive cone fixture is
A=1, Bv=2, C=2, d=2.
Then ABv+AC+BvC=8=2d^2, exactly two gaps are even, gcd(A,Bv,C)=1, and
(s,t,u)=(3,3,4),
(H_A,H_B,H_C)=(9,12,12),
(rad(H_A),rad(H_B),rad(H_C))=(3,6,6).
Their radical product is 108, not a square.
This fixture is NOT asserted to be a perfect-cuboid endpoint. It is sufficient to invalidate the previous algebraic inference from the cone identity alone; no retained physical theorem establishing the missing coprimality was found.
RESULT_229BZ_BY_RADICAL_THREE_ATOM_INFERENCE=RETRACTED_SCOPED.
The correct valuation-parity statement is instead
sf(H_A) sf(H_B) sf(H_C) is a square,
where sf denotes the parity squarefree kernel. This is structural only and is not substituted for the radical receiver used in the hard13 counting reduction.


3. Primitive pair-sum gcd
229BX gives gcd(A,Bv,C)=1 and exactly two of A,Bv,C even. Hence exactly one of s,t,u is even and the other two are odd.
If g divides s,t,u, then g is odd and
g | (s+t-u)=2A,
g | (s+u-t)=2Bv,
g | (t+u-s)=2C.
Thus g|gcd(A,Bv,C)=1 and
gcd(s,t,u)=1.                                                   (BZ.1)
Consequently no prime divides all three pair sums. The three pairwise gcds
g_st=gcd(s,t), g_su=gcd(s,u), g_tu=gcd(t,u)
have pairwise coprime supports.


4. Exact four-atom decomposition of the three radicals
Set
k_A=rad(H_A)=rad(st),
k_B=rad(H_B)=rad(su),
k_C=rad(H_C)=rad(tu).
Define the common atom
tau=gcd(k_A,k_B,k_C).
By (BZ.1), a prime belongs to tau exactly when it divides exactly two of s,t,u. Therefore
tau=rad(g_st g_su g_tu).                                      (BZ.2)
Define
v_s=gcd(k_A,k_B)/tau,
v_t=gcd(k_A,k_C)/tau,
v_u=gcd(k_B,k_C)/tau.                                         (BZ.3)
Then tau,v_s,v_t,v_u are pairwise coprime squarefree integers and exactly
k_A=tau v_s v_t,
k_B=tau v_s v_u,
k_C=tau v_t v_u.                                              (BZ.4)
Equivalently
k_A k_B k_C=tau^3 (v_s v_t v_u)^2,                            (BZ.5)
so the old three-atom formula is valid if and only if tau=1.
If v_(1)<=v_(2)<=v_(3) are v_s,v_t,v_u in increasing order, the simultaneous hard13 inequalities
k_A>T, k_B>T, k_C>T
are exactly equivalent to
tau v_(1) v_(2)>T.                                            (BZ.6)

5. Arithmetic localization of the common atom
Let p be an odd prime dividing tau. By symmetry suppose p|s and p|t. Then
Bv==C==-A mod p.
If p divided A, it would divide A,Bv,C, contradicting gcd(A,Bv,C)=1. Thus p does not divide ABC.
Reducing the cone equation gives

Hence p does not divide d and

Therefore (-2/p)=1, equivalently
p == 1 or 3 mod 8.                                            (BZ.8)
Also tau is odd because exactly one of s,t,u is even.
Thus

Every prime of the retained 229BX overlap conductor Q=q_UV q_Uz q_Vz divides at least two of A,Bv,C. Since every p|tau divides none of A,Bv,C,
gcd(tau,Q)=1.                                                 (BZ.10)

6. Correct squareclass triangle
Put
sigma_A=sf(H_A), sigma_B=sf(H_B), sigma_C=sf(H_C).
Because v_p(H_A)+v_p(H_B)+v_p(H_C) is even for every prime p, exactly

Thus the parity squareclasses have a genuine three-atom decomposition with no common atom.
This does NOT imply a B^o(1) fixed-sigma physical fiber and supplies no independent counting saving. The hard13 receiver remains based on radicals k_A,k_B,k_C, whose correct structure is (BZ.4).

What changes is only the internal support description: hard13 now carries the exact four-atom condition tau v_(1)v_(2)>T, not the retracted radical three-atom condition.
The new cross-structure with 229BX is

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BX — exact square overlap conductors and desaturated outer-gap cone budget

PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope and notation
Use exactly the current positive primitive Stage37 physical endpoints, with all selectors and R<=B:
x²+y²=z², e²+z²=R², e²+x²=U², e²+y²=V², gcd(e,x,y)=1.
Retain A=R-U, C=R-z, and write Bv=R-V to avoid confusion with the height bound B. All are positive.
Retain229BU D=R-A-Bv-C>0, D²=2(ABv+AC+BvC), R=A+Bv+C+D.
For positive n, odd(n)=n/2^v2(n). Retain229BW chi and unique atoms u_U,u_V,u_z. Retain d0=gcd(x,y), a=gcd(e,y), b=gcd(e,x).


2. Exact odd pair-gcd square theorem
Define
q_UV=sqrt(odd(gcd(A,Bv))),
q_Uz=sqrt(odd(gcd(A,C))),
q_Vz=sqrt(odd(gcd(Bv,C))).
These square roots are integers, not merely formal radicals.


Proof for q_UV:
An odd prime p dividing A and Bv divides y and x because
A(R+U)=y² and Bv(R+V)=x².
Such p cannot divide R: otherwise e²=R²-x²-y² implies p|e, contradicting primitive edges. Hence R,U,V are units modulo p and R+U,R+V are units modulo p. Consequently
v_p(A)=2v_p(y), v_p(Bv)=2v_p(x),
v_p(gcd(A,Bv))=2v_p(d0).
This proves that the odd gcd is square and that q_UV is the full prime-power subproduct of odd(d0) on precisely those primes for which R≡U≡V mod p. In particular q_UV|d0 and gcd(q_UV,R)=1.
The other two cases are identical:
at p|gcd(A,C), v_p(A)=2v_p(y), v_p(C)=2v_p(e), giving q_Uz|a;
at p|gcd(Bv,C), v_p(Bv)=2v_p(x), v_p(C)=2v_p(e), giving q_Vz|b.
By229BW/229BI, these three odd conductors are pairwise coprime. They need not be squarefree. They select full valuations from d0,a,b; they do not equal the whole buckets in general.
RESULT_229BX_ODD_OUTER_PAIR_GCDS_ARE_EXACT_SQUARES=PROVED.
RESULT_229BX_ODD_OVERLAP_CONDUCTORS_SELECT_FULL_CONTENT_VALUATIONS=PROVED.


3. Exact prime-2 bit and common support
The face equations modulo4 allow at most one odd edge among e,x,y. Primitivity forces at least one odd edge. Therefore exactly one edge is odd and R is odd.
Exactly two of U,V,z are odd and one is even. Thus exactly two of A,Bv,C are even, and the third is odd.
There is no odd triple overlap by229BW. Therefore
gcd(A,Bv,C)=1,
chi=2 rad(Q), where Q=q_UV q_Uz q_Vz.                         (BX.1)
This refines229BW's previously unspecified prime-2 bit. It does not assert that the even part of any individual pair gcd is square.
RESULT_229BX_CHI_EQUALS_TWO_TIMES_ODD_OVERLAP_CONDUCTOR_RADICAL=PROVED.


4. Remove shared square conductors from the exact cone
Write canonically
A=q_UV² q_Uz² A0,
Bv=q_UV² q_Vz² B0,
C=q_Uz² q_Vz² C0.                                           (BX.2)
Each residual is a positive integer. The residuals are pairwise coprime at odd primes:
odd(gcd(A0,B0))=odd(gcd(A0,C0))=odd(gcd(B0,C0))=1.            (BX.3)
Indeed, for any shared odd prime the full minimum valuation was removed from both affected gaps. No new common prime can be introduced by division.


Every term ABv,AC,BvC is divisible by Q², so the exact cone gives Q²|D² and hence Q|D. Put D0=D/Q, a positive integer. Dividing yields
D0²=2(q_UV² A0 B0 + q_Uz² A0 C0 + q_Vz² B0 C0),            (BX.4)
R=q_UV² q_Uz² A0+q_UV² q_Vz² B0+q_Uz² q_Vz² C0+Q D0.       (BX.5)
This is a canonical injective endpoint representation: the six labelled integers q_UV,q_Uz,q_Vz,A0,B0,C0 determine D0 if it exists, then the original gaps, R,U,V,z, and e,x,y uniquely on the positive physical chamber by229BU.


Important precision: (BX.3) does NOT imply gcd(Q,A0B0C0)=1. If the two original gap valuations are unequal, the larger gap retains an excess valuation after removing the common square. These excess primes may still divide Q.
With rad_odd(n) the odd support, the unique atom is exactly
u_U=rad_odd(A0)/gcd(rad_odd(A0),rad(Q)),
and cyclically for u_V from B0 and u_z from C0. All unique atoms are odd since 2 lies in chi.
RESULT_229BX_EXACT_DESATURATED_WEIGHTED_OUTER_GAP_CONE=PROVED.
RESULT_229BX_RESIDUES_PAIRWISE_ODD_COPRIME_WITH_CONDUCTOR_EXCESS_FIREWALL=PROVED.


5. Exact quartic cost and height bounds
Multiplication of (BX.2) gives
Omega=ABvC=Q^4 A0B0C0.                                      (BX.6)
Since A+Bv+C<R, AM-GM yields
Q^4 A0B0C0 < R³/27 <= B³/27,
Q < B^(3/4)/27^(1/4),
D0 < B/Q.                                                  (BX.7)
Thus large overlap has an exact quartic cost in the gap-product budget, stronger than support-only localization. These are deterministic inequalities; no density factor is inferred.


6. Attempted large-overlap count: valid but insufficient
Let N_chi(B;K) count whole physical endpoints R<=B with chi>K, K>=2. The same upper bound applies to the hard10 subsource.
By (BX.1), Q>K/2. For each Q, the number of labelled conductor factorizations is at most d3(Q). For each such factorization, (BX.7) bounds the number of positive labelled residual triples by
sum_{n<=B³/(27Q^4)} d3(n) << (B³/Q^4) B^o(1).
Endpoint injectivity from section4 then gives, for every fixed epsilon>0,
N_chi(B;K) <<_epsilon B^(3+epsilon) K^(-3).                 (BX.8)
We intentionally drop the weighted cone equation and physical selectors only in deriving this upper bound; it is not a replacement source.


At the229BW branch cutoff K=T^alpha, T=B^(1/3-delta), the resulting exponent is
3-alpha+3alpha*delta+epsilon.
At alpha=1/3 this is 8/3+delta+epsilon, vastly above1/3.
For K=B^kappa, this coarse bound would require kappa>8/9 to yield a fixed-power bound below B^(1/3), whereas nonempty conductors satisfy Q<<B^(3/4), and chi<=2Q. Therefore the product-budget-only summation cannot meet the one-third target in its nonempty polynomial-scale range. This is a diagnosis of (BX.8), not a no-go theorem for a sharper weighted-cone/selector count.
RESULT_229BX_COARSE_OVERLAP_PRODUCT_BUDGET_COUNT=PROVED_BOUND_QUANTITATIVELY_TOO_WEAK.
No additional o(B^(1/3)) sector is disposed.


7. Current contract
The source remains exactly S_B^hard10(delta) from229BV; no condition is removed or newly charged.
Retain large sf(G0), all seven physical-length radicals high, and the exact229BW pair condition chi*u_(1)*u_(2)>T.
