﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BW — outer-gap radical support triangle and six-bucket overlap localization


STATUS: POST_229BV_OUTER_GAP_SUPPORT_TRIANGLE / EXACT_FOUR_ATOM_PAIR_RADICAL_DECOMPOSITION / ODD_TRIPLE_OVERLAP_EMPTY / ODD_PAIR_OVERLAPS_LOCALIZED_TO_D0_A_B / SPLIT_BUCKET_SUPPORT_EMBEDDED_IN_THREE_UNIQUE_ATOMS / HARD10_PAIR_PART_COMPRESSED_TO_ONE_FOUR_ATOM_INEQUALITY / NO_COUNTING_PROMOTION / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
TYPE: post-229BV exact prime-support correlation / outer-gap Venn decomposition / six-content-bucket crosswalk / hard10 theorem-interface refinement
CARD_DOC_ID=1s3DDDk20syUfEEtxuNk7SYUvAnF9XEqlWp0nRqIr6ww
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED; PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope


Work on exactly the current positive primitive Stage37 physical endpoints P with all original selectors and R(P)<=B.


Retain 229BL/229BV notation
  g_U := R-U >0,
  g_V := R-V >0,
  g_z := R-z >0,                                      (229BW.1)
and the three squarefree pair-support receivers
  r_e := rad(g_U g_V),
  r_y := rad(g_z g_V),
  r_x := rad(g_z g_U).                                (229BW.2)


Retain 229AD/229BI's six pairwise-coprime physical content buckets
  h   = gcd(e,R)=gcd(e,z),
  d0  = gcd(x,y),
  a   = gcd(e,y),
  b   = gcd(e,x),
  c12 = gcd(y,R)=gcd(U,y),
  c21 = gcd(x,R)=gcd(V,x),                            (229BW.3)
with h,d0,a,b,c12,c21 pairwise coprime. Retain that h,c12,c21 are odd and have only split odd prime support.


This card does not count hard10. It proves the exact correlation structure among the three 229BV pair-radical masks.


2. Canonical four-atom decomposition of the three pair radicals


Define
  chi := gcd(r_e,r_y,r_x),                            (229BW.4)
and
  u_U := gcd(r_e,r_x)/chi,
  u_V := gcd(r_e,r_y)/chi,
  u_z := gcd(r_y,r_x)/chi.                           (229BW.5)


All four quantities are squarefree positive integers. Prime-by-prime:
- chi consists exactly of primes dividing at least two of g_U,g_V,g_z;
- u_U consists exactly of primes dividing g_U and neither g_V nor g_z;
- u_V consists exactly of primes dividing g_V and neither g_U nor g_z;
- u_z consists exactly of primes dividing g_z and neither g_U nor g_V.


Hence
  gcd(chi,u_U u_V u_z)=1,
  gcd(u_U,u_V)=gcd(u_V,u_z)=gcd(u_z,u_U)=1.          (229BW.6)


The three pair radicals reconstruct exactly as
  r_e = chi u_U u_V,
  r_y = chi u_V u_z,
  r_x = chi u_z u_U.                                (229BW.7)


Also
  rad(g_U g_V g_z)=chi u_U u_V u_z,                 (229BW.8)
and therefore
  r_e r_y r_x
    = chi^3 u_U^2 u_V^2 u_z^2
    = chi [rad(g_U g_V g_z)]^2.                     (229BW.9)


Equivalently,
  (r_e r_y r_x)/chi
is an exact integer square.


RESULT_229BW_OUTER_PAIR_RADICALS_HAVE_EXACT_FOUR_ATOM_SUPPORT_TRIANGLE=PROVED.
RESULT_229BW_PAIR_RADICAL_PRODUCT_OVER_COMMON_OVERLAP_IS_EXACT_SQUARE=PROVED.


This is an exact dependence relation. The three pair-radical masks are not independent.


3. Physical localization of odd pair overlaps


For a positive integer n write rad_odd(n) for the product of its odd prime divisors.


Let p be odd.


If p|g_U and p|g_V, then p|R-U and p|R-V, so U≡V≡R mod p. Using
  R^2-U^2=y^2,
  R^2-V^2=x^2,
we get p|x and p|y. Therefore
  p|d0=gcd(x,y).                                    (229BW.10)


If p|g_U and p|g_z, then U≡z≡R mod p. From
  R^2-U^2=y^2,
  R^2-z^2=e^2,
we obtain p|e,y and therefore
  p|a=gcd(e,y).                                     (229BW.11)


If p|g_V and p|g_z, similarly
  p|b=gcd(e,x).                                     (229BW.12)


Define the three odd overlap atoms
  chi_UV := rad_odd(gcd(g_U,g_V)),
  chi_Uz := rad_odd(gcd(g_U,g_z)),
  chi_Vz := rad_odd(gcd(g_V,g_z)).                 (229BW.13)


Then exactly
  chi_UV | rad(d0),
  chi_Uz | rad(a),
  chi_Vz | rad(b).                                 (229BW.14)


Because d0,a,b are pairwise coprime by 229AD, the three odd overlap atoms in (229BW.13) are pairwise coprime. In particular no odd prime can divide all three outer gaps:
  rad_odd(gcd(g_U,g_V,g_z))=1.                     (229BW.15)


Thus the odd part of the common pair-radical overlap is
  chi_odd = chi_UV chi_Uz chi_Vz,                  (229BW.16)
with the three factors supported respectively in the unrestricted content buckets d0,a,b.


RESULT_229BW_ODD_TRIPLE_OUTER_GAP_OVERLAP_EMPTY=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229BW_ODD_PAIR_OVERLAPS_LOCALIZED_TO_D0_A_B=PROVED_EXACT.


No assertion is made about the prime 2 beyond the generic four-atom decomposition.


4. Split-only content buckets lie in three distinct unique atoms


Retain the pairwise-content property of integral Pythagorean triples:
- (U,y,R) has content c12, so gcd(U,R)=gcd(y,R)=c12;
- (V,x,R) has content c21, so gcd(V,R)=gcd(x,R)=c21;
- (e,z,R) has content h, so gcd(z,R)=gcd(e,R)=h.    (229BW.17)


Let p be an odd prime dividing c12. Then p|R and p|U, so p|g_U.
Pairwise coprimality gives p∤c21 and p∤h. Hence p∤V and p∤z by (229BW.17), so p∤g_V and p∤g_z.
Therefore p belongs to the unique g_U atom u_U.


Thus
  rad(c12) | u_U.                                  (229BW.18)


Similarly,
  rad(c21) | u_V,                                  (229BW.19)
  rad(h)   | u_z.                                  (229BW.20)


Here h,c12,c21 are odd, so no 2-adic qualification is needed for these inclusions.


RESULT_229BW_SPLIT_BUCKET_C12_EMBEDS_IN_UNIQUE_U_ATOM=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229BW_SPLIT_BUCKET_C21_EMBEDS_IN_UNIQUE_V_ATOM=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229BW_SPLIT_BUCKET_H_EMBEDS_IN_UNIQUE_Z_ATOM=PROVED_EXACT.


This is an inclusion, not equality. The unique atoms may contain additional primes coming from the square multipliers in the physical Pythagorean gap factorizations. In particular it is invalid to replace u_U,u_V,u_z by rad(c12),rad(c21),rad(h).


5. Exact six-bucket/outer-support crosswalk


The odd support picture is therefore:


overlap support:
  chi_UV -> d0,
  chi_Uz -> a,
  chi_Vz -> b;                                     (229BW.21)


forced unique split support:
  c12 -> u_U,
  c21 -> u_V,
  h   -> u_z.                                      (229BW.22)


Thus the 229AD six pairwise-coprime buckets split naturally across the outer-gap Venn diagram:
- unrestricted buckets d0,a,b are the only possible hosts for odd support shared by two outer gaps;
- split-only buckets c12,c21,h are forced into three distinct one-gap-only components.


This is a new exact crosswalk between the 229AD/229BI content packet and the 229BV hard10 pair-radical masks.


RESULT_229BW_SIX_BUCKET_OUTER_GAP_VENN_CROSSWALK=PROVED_EXACT.


This does NOT say that every prime of d0,a,b occurs in an overlap, nor that the unique atoms contain only h,c12,c21.


6. Compress the three hard10 pair-radical inequalities


Let
  T=B^(1/3-delta)
for the current fixed delta.


The pair-radical portion of hard10 is
  r_e>T, r_y>T, r_x>T.                             (229BW.23)


Using (229BW.7), this is exactly
  chi u_U u_V > T,
  chi u_V u_z > T,
  chi u_z u_U > T.                                (229BW.24)


Order the three unique atoms numerically:
  u_(1) <= u_(2) <= u_(3).


Then the smallest of the three products in (229BW.24) is
  chi u_(1)u_(2).
Therefore the entire three-mask condition is equivalent to the single inequality
  chi u_(1)u_(2) > T.                              (229BW.25)


RESULT_229BW_HARD10_THREE_PAIR_RADICAL_CONDITIONS_COMPRESS_TO_ONE_FOUR_ATOM_INEQUALITY=PROVED_EXACT.


This is compression of dependent conditions, not a counting saving.


A useful deterministic split follows. For any fixed alpha in [0,1], every endpoint satisfying (229BW.25) lies in one of:
  chi > T^alpha,                                   (229BW.26)
or
  u_(2) > T^((1-alpha)/2) and
  u_(3) > T^((1-alpha)/2).                        (229BW.27)


Indeed, if chi<=T^alpha, then u_(1)u_(2)>T^(1-alpha); since u_(1)<=u_(2), this forces u_(2)>T^((1-alpha)/2), and u_(3)>=u_(2).


At alpha=1/3:
  either chi>T^(1/3),
  or at least two unique atoms exceed T^(1/3).     (229BW.28)


At the current T=B^(1/3-delta), the atom threshold in (229BW.28) is
  B^(1/9-delta/3).


RESULT_229BW_HARD10_OVERLAP_VS_TWO_UNIQUE_ATOMS_DICHOTOMY=PROVED_EXACT_STRUCTURAL.


No endpoint count follows from this dichotomy without a same-physical support theorem.


7. Consequence for the current source and theorem input


The current source remains exactly S_B^hard10(delta) from229BV:
- exact positive primitive Stage37 selectors and R<=B;
- sf(G0)>B^(1/3-delta);
- all seven physical-length radicals >T;
- all three outer pair radicals >T.


229BW does not remove an additional sector. Instead it replaces the last three conditions by the exact four-atom support object
  (chi,u_U,u_V,u_z)
with (229BW.25), and supplies the content localization (229BW.21)-(229BW.22).


CURRENT_PREFERRED_NEW_INTERNAL_INTERFACE:
  229BW_OUTER_GAP_FOUR_ATOM_SUPPORT_TRIANGLE_ON_HARD10.

Prove #S_B^hard10(delta)=o(B^(1/3)) by exploiting the exact four-atom support correlation, or prove a fixed-power realized-support bound for retained rho/sigma on this same source. A promising internal split is:
(A) large chi branch, where odd common overlap can only be carried by a,b,d0;
(B) two-large-unique-atoms branch, where the three distinct unique atoms already contain rad(c12),rad(c21),rad(h) respectively.
Any count must retain exact physical selectors and the 229BU outer-gap cone. Do not multiply the three pair-radical masks as independent events.


8. Firewalls


Do not:
- treat r_e,r_y,r_x as independent;
- infer a fixed-power saving from (r_e r_y r_x)/chi being square;
- replace chi by rad(a b d0), since only divisibility/localization is proved;

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229BV — three outer-pair radical fibers and hard10 reduction


STATUS: POST_229BU_THREE_OUTER_PAIR_PRODUCTS_FIXED_FIBER_B_O / THREE_OUTER_PAIR_RADICAL_FIXED_FIBER_B_O / K10_LOW_RADICAL_SECTOR_O_T_B_O / HARD10_SOURCE_EQUIVALENCE / HARD10_SUBSUMES_229BU_HARD8_AND_229BL_PAIR_SIZE_REMAINDER / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN
TYPE: post-229BU exact 229BL divisor-chart extraction / three pair-product finite-fiber receivers / radical-support sector disposal / stronger source narrowing
CARD_DOC_ID=1zkCxqOjfD0xOMDFEw0iKzOxWU1XzHBw5hd-uZc9DGIM
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY=M3-T11-229; LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION=M3-T11-228; M3-T11-230 NOT_ISSUED; PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN; GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false; PRODUCTION HOLD.


1. Scope


Use exactly the current positive primitive Stage37 physical endpoints P with all original selector conditions and R(P)<=B.


Retain 229BL:
  A := R-U >0,
  Bv := R-V >0,
  C := R-z >0,                                      (229BV.1)
and the three exact divisor charts
  lambda_e(2e+lambda_e)=2 A Bv,
  lambda_y(2y+lambda_y)=2 C Bv,
  lambda_x(2x+lambda_x)=2 C A.                    (229BV.2)


For fixed positive (A,Bv,lambda_e), the e-chart reconstructs the whole labelled endpoint uniquely if physical; likewise fixed (C,Bv,lambda_y) and fixed (C,A,lambda_x). This is the retained 229BL endpoint-fiber-at-most-one statement.


Retain 229BT:
  k7(P)=min{rad(e),rad(x),rad(y),rad(z),rad(U),rad(V),rad(R)}
has uniform B^o fixed-value physical fibers.


Retain 229BQ's uniform prescribed-prime-support lemma for polynomial-height integers.


2. Fixed outer pair product has B^o physical fiber


Define the three labelled pair products
  Q_e := A Bv = (R-U)(R-V),
  Q_y := C Bv = (R-z)(R-V),
  Q_x := C A  = (R-z)(R-U).                       (229BV.3)


Each Q_j is a positive integer <B^2.


Fix n>=1 and first consider Q_e=n. The ordered positive factorization A Bv=n has at most tau(n) choices.


For each such factorization, (229BV.2) gives
  lambda_e | 2n.
Hence lambda_e has at most tau(2n) possible positive values.


For each triple (A,Bv,lambda_e), the retained 229BL reconstruction is injective:
  e=(2ABv/lambda_e-lambda_e)/2,
  U=e+Bv+lambda_e,
  V=e+A+lambda_e,
  R=e+A+Bv+lambda_e,
and then x,y,z are uniquely forced if integral and physical.
All selector, parity, primitivity and canonical-orientation conditions only remove candidates.


Therefore
  #{P:R<=B,Q_e(P)=n}
    <= tau(n) tau(2n)
    = B^o(1),                                      (229BV.4)
uniformly for n<=B^2.


The identical y- and x-chart arguments give
  #{P:R<=B,Q_y(P)=n} <= B^o(1),
  #{P:R<=B,Q_x(P)=n} <= B^o(1).                    (229BV.5)


RESULT_229BV_THREE_OUTER_PAIR_PRODUCT_FIXED_VALUE_FIBERS_B_O=PROVED_EXACT_FROM_229BL.


This is stronger than merely summing Q_j<=H as in 229BL: it isolates a uniform fixed-value fiber theorem for each pair-product scalar.


3. Fixed radical of each outer pair product also has B^o fiber


Define squarefree pair-support receivers
  r_e(P):=rad(Q_e(P)),
  r_y(P):=rad(Q_y(P)),
  r_x(P):=rad(Q_x(P)).                             (229BV.6)


Fix a squarefree s. Any Q_j<=B^2 with rad(Q_j)=s has all prime divisors in the prescribed support s. By 229BQ, uniformly in s, there are only B^o possible Q_j values of polynomial height.


Each fixed Q_j value has B^o physical preimages by (229BV.4)-(229BV.5). Therefore
  #{P:R<=B,r_e(P)=s} <= B^o(1),
  #{P:R<=B,r_y(P)=s} <= B^o(1),
  #{P:R<=B,r_x(P)=s} <= B^o(1),                   (229BV.7)
uniformly in squarefree s.


RESULT_229BV_THREE_OUTER_PAIR_RADICAL_FIXED_VALUE_FIBERS_B_O=PROVED.


No independence of the three pair radicals is used or claimed.


4. One combined ten-receiver minimum


Define
  k10(P):=min{
    rad(e),rad(x),rad(y),rad(z),rad(U),rad(V),rad(R),
    r_e,r_y,r_x
  }.                                               (229BV.8)


For fixed squarefree s, the event k10(P)=s is contained in a union of ten fixed-receiver events. The seven physical-length events have B^o fibers by 229BT and the three pair-radical events have B^o fibers by (229BV.7). Hence
  #{P:R<=B,k10(P)=s} <= B^o(1).                    (229BV.9)


Consequently, for every T>=1,
  #{P:R<=B,k10(P)<=T} << T B^o(1).                 (229BV.10)


For any fixed 0<delta<1/3, taking
  T=B^(1/3-delta)
gives
  #{P:R<=B,k10(P)<=B^(1/3-delta)}
    =O(B^(1/3-delta+o(1)))
    =o(B^(1/3)).                                   (229BV.11)


RESULT_229BV_K10_FIXED_VALUE_FIBER_B_O=PROVED.
RESULT_229BV_K10_LOW_RADICAL_SECTOR_O_B13=PROVED_SCOPED.


This is one union-bound count through a single-valued minimum receiver. It does not multiply ten sieve densities.


5. Hard10 source and exact gate reduction


Retain the original current large-squarefree source
  S_B(delta)
   ={P:R<=B, positive primitive Stage37 endpoint with all selectors,
       sf(G0(P))>B^(1/3-delta)}.


Define
  S_B^hard10(delta)
   ={P in S_B(delta):
       rad(e),rad(x),rad(y),rad(z),rad(U),rad(V),rad(R)>B^(1/3-delta),
       rad((R-U)(R-V))>B^(1/3-delta),
       rad((R-z)(R-V))>B^(1/3-delta),
       rad((R-z)(R-U))>B^(1/3-delta)}.             (229BV.12)


The complement inside S_B(delta) is contained in the global low-k10 sector (229BV.11), so
  |S_B(delta)|
   =|S_B^hard10(delta)|
      +O(B^(1/3-delta+o(1))).                     (229BV.13)


Thus, at the same fixed delta,
  |S_B^hard10(delta)|=o(B^(1/3))                  (229BV.14)
is necessary and sufficient for the original preferred large-sf(G0) tail theorem.


RESULT_229BV_GATE_REDUCTION_TO_HARD10=PROVED_EXACT_UP_TO_o_B13.


The hard10 estimate itself is NOT proved.


6. hard10 strictly strengthens the current structural remainder


First, hard10 automatically implies the 229BU outer-product-radical condition. Indeed
  rad((R-U)(R-V))
    divides rad((R-U)(R-V)(R-z)).
Hence if even one pair radical is >T, then the triple-product radical is >T; hard10 requires all three pair radicals >T. Therefore
  S_B^hard10(delta) subset S_B^hard8(delta).       (229BV.15)


Second, since rad(n)<=n,
  rad((R-U)(R-V))>T => (R-U)(R-V)>T,
and cyclically. Thus with eta=delta, every hard10 endpoint automatically lies in the retained 229BL all-three-pair-large remainder:
  (R-U)(R-V)>B^(1/3-delta),
  (R-z)(R-V)>B^(1/3-delta),
  (R-z)(R-U)>B^(1/3-delta).                       (229BV.16)


Therefore the 229BU hard8 condition and the separately retained 229BL pair-size-hard condition no longer need to be carried as additional hypotheses once hard10 is imposed.


RESULT_229BV_HARD10_SUBSUMES_229BU_HARD8=PROVED.
RESULT_229BV_HARD10_SUBSUMES_229BL_PAIR_SIZE_HARD_REMAINDER_AT_ETA_EQUALS_DELTA=PROVED.


No claim is made that the inclusion is physically strict on an actually nonempty perfect-cuboid population.


7. Consequences for retained rho/sigma interfaces


Restrict the retained 229BR receiver images to hard10:
  T_rho^hard10(B;delta)={rho(P):P in S_B^hard10(delta)},
  T_sigma^hard10(B;delta)={sigma(P):P in S_B^hard10(delta)}.


Their whole-physical fixed-value B^o fiber bounds survive restriction. Therefore either
  #T_rho^hard10(B;delta) << B^(1/3-epsilon)
or
  #T_sigma^hard10(B;delta) << B^(1/3-epsilon)
for some fixed epsilon>0
would imply (229BV.14).


The exact 229BU outer-gap cone
  D^2=2(ABv+AC+BvC)
remains valid on hard10, now together with all three pair-product radical lower bounds. No occupied-support saving is proved here.


8. Current blocker and next research contract


CURRENT_PREFERRED_NEW_INTERNAL_INTERFACE:
  229BV_K10_LOW_RADICAL_DISPOSAL_AND_HARD10_THREE_PAIR_SUPPORT_REMAINDER.


CURRENT_SCOPED_BLOCKER:

- all three outer pair-product radicals >B^(1/3-delta);

- the exact 229BU quadratic outer-gap cone.


A useful next direction is a genuine global correlation among the three pair-supports on the physical cone, or a selector-aware occupied-support theorem for rho/sigma after this stronger source restriction.

- multiply their local densities;

  k7(P)=min{rad(e),rad(x),rad(y),rad(z),rad(U),rad(V),rad(R)}
has uniform B^o(1) fixed-value physical fibers and
  #{P:R<=B,k7(P)<=T} << T B^o(1).                    (229BU.1)


Retain 229BL's three positive outer gaps
  A := R-U,
  Bv := R-V,
  C := R-z.                                           (229BU.2)
They satisfy A,Bv,C>0. This card does not use them as three independent filters. Instead it reconstructs an endpoint from the labelled triple (A,Bv,C), then compresses the triple to one multiplicative radical receiver.


Notation: rad(n) is the product of all distinct prime divisors of n. It is not the squarefree kernel sf(n).


2. Exact outer-gap quadratic reconstruction


From
  e^2+x^2=U^2,
  e^2+y^2=V^2,
  x^2+y^2=z^2,
  e^2+z^2=R^2,
and (229BU.2),
  y^2 = R^2-U^2 = A(2R-A),                         (229BU.3)
  x^2 = R^2-V^2 = Bv(2R-Bv),                       (229BU.4)
  e^2 = R^2-z^2 = C(2R-C).                         (229BU.5)


Using x^2+y^2=z^2=(R-C)^2 gives
  A(2R-A)+Bv(2R-Bv)=(R-C)^2.
Equivalently
  R^2-2R(A+Bv+C)+(A^2+Bv^2+C^2)=0.                (229BU.6)


Let
  S=A+Bv+C.
Then
  (R-S)^2 = 2(ABv+AC+BvC).                         (229BU.7)


The sign is fixed physically. Indeed
  R-S=U+V+z-2R
     =(U+V-R-e)+(e+z-R).
The first parenthesis is lambda_e>0 by the retained 229BL central-gap theorem, and the second is >0 because R^2=e^2+z^2 with e,z>0. Hence
  R-S = sqrt(2(ABv+AC+BvC)) >0,                    (229BU.8)
so for a fixed labelled positive triple (A,Bv,C), R is uniquely determined:
  R = A+Bv+C + sqrt(2(ABv+AC+BvC)).                (229BU.9)


Once R is fixed,
  U=R-A, V=R-Bv, z=R-C,
and e,x,y are the unique positive square roots in (229BU.3)-(229BU.5), if those quantities are integral squares. All primitivity, selector, orientation and remaining consistency conditions only discard candidates.


Therefore
  #{P:R(P)<=B,(R-U,R-V,R-z)=(A,Bv,C)} <= 1.        (229BU.10)

3. Fixed outer-gap product has subpower physical fiber


Define
  Omega(P):=(R-U)(R-V)(R-z)=A Bv C.                (229BU.11)


For a fixed positive integer n, the number of labelled positive triples
  A Bv C=n
is at most the ordered ternary divisor count d_3(n). By the standard uniform divisor bound, for n<=B^3,
  d_3(n)=B^o(1).


Each labelled triple has physical fiber at most one by (229BU.10). Therefore uniformly in n,
  #{P:R<=B,Omega(P)=n} <= B^o(1).                  (229BU.12)


For completeness, Omega has polynomial height. From (229BU.3)-(229BU.5),
  A=y^2/(R+U),
  Bv=x^2/(R+V),
  C=e^2/(R+z).
Hence
  Omega = e^2 x^2 y^2 / ((R+U)(R+V)(R+z))
        < e^2 x^2 y^2/R^3.
Since e^2+x^2+y^2=R^2, AM-GM gives
  e^2 x^2 y^2 <= R^6/27,
therefore
  Omega < R^3/27 <= B^3/27.                        (229BU.13)

4. Fixed radical of the product also has subpower fiber


Define the squarefree support scalar
  k_gap(P):=rad(Omega(P)).                          (229BU.14)


Fix squarefree s. Every possible Omega(P)<=B^3/27 with rad(Omega)=s is an integer of polynomial height whose prime divisors all lie in the prescribed support s.


Retain the uniform prescribed-prime-support lemma used in 229BQ and 229BT: for fixed height exponent, the number of polynomial-height integers supported on a prescribed squarefree integer is B^o(1), uniformly in that support.


Thus for fixed s there are B^o(1) possible Omega values. Combining with (229BU.12),
  #{P:R<=B,k_gap(P)=s} <= B^o(1),                  (229BU.15)
uniformly in s.

  #{P:R<=B,k_gap(P)<=T} << T B^o(1).               (229BU.16)
